body_preview:
This mail is sent with contacts in BCC as a reminder regarding parts training. The first session took place on July 29.

We kindly ask you to register for one of the next dates by confirming in reaction to this email

 

 

Dear Distributors,

 

We are pleased to inform you that the next ISUZU e-learning and information sessions covering EDI and Order Types & Procedures have been scheduled on the following dates:

 

*	Wednesday, 26 August
*	Wednesday, 23 September

 

During these sessions, we will explain the available order types, EDI possibilities, the implementation process, and best practices to help you optimize your ordering process with Isuzu Motors Europe.

 

To allow us to organize the sessions efficiently, please reply to this email and let us know which of the above sessions you and your colleagues would like to attend.

In addition, we would like to remind you of the previously launched EQ-Hit Parts Training. We kindly ask you to actively encourage all relevant dealership personnel to complete both the training and the online test if they have not already done so.

 

The training can be accessed via the following link:

https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=iWq0MnaF3Um94p3g8iE-yJV6ECXpY79Gt108WtczF09UMllWSk5PSDNWVVFPNlJDNkxaT0NWMllPRi4u&route=shorturl

 

This training has been developed to strengthen parts knowledge, improve the use of EQ-Hit, and ultimately support the growth of genuine parts sales throughout our dealer network.

 

Please note that completion of this training is mandatory and forms part of the requirements for the Isuzu Dealer Standards Awarding. Your support in ensuring that your dealerships participate is therefore greatly appreciated.

 

Should you have any questions regarding either the EDI sessions or the EQ-Hit training, please do not hesitate to contact us.

 

Thank you for your continued cooperation and support.

1. ISZE System Unavailability 

 

We have received confirmation from Isuzu Japan's ICT Department regarding a planned system outage.

As a result, our systems will be unavailable from Monday morning until Tuesday evening.  Consequently:

*	New orders cannot be processed on Monday and Tuesday.
*	The web ordering portal will be completely unavailable.
*	Warehouse operations and invoicing activities will also be suspended during this period.

 

Should the web portal appear to be operational during this period, we kindly ask you not to place any orders, as we cannot guarantee that they will be received or processed correctly.

To ensure proper processing, please submit any new orders from Wednesday at 09:00 onwards.

EDI orders can be placed but they will be frozen until all systems are back online.

Furthermore, any information displayed may not reflect real-time data and should therefore not be considered fully up to date.

 

We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

 

2. Isuzu Japan Closure

Isuzu Japan will be closed from 8 August until 16 August 2026.

Consequently, shipments from the supplier may be delayed during this period, and lead times for backordered items may be affected accordingly.

 

3. ISZE Closure on Friday

Please also note that ISZE will be closed on Friday, 14 August 2026, in observance of the Assumption Day holiday on Saturday, 15 August 2026.

 

We understand that these temporary disruptions may create additional challenges for your business, and we sincerely appreciate your patience, flexibility, and understanding during this period. 

Please be assured that our team is closely monitoring the situation and doing everything possible to minimise any impact on your operations and maintain the highest level of service.

Your business is important to us, and we remain committed to supporting you throughout this period. 

Thank you for your continued trust and cooperation.

 

Should you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us.

 

 

 

   Kind regards,

Koen Matheussen

Assistant Manager

subject: Important Information Regarding System Downtime and Operational Impact
body_preview:
Dear Valued Customer,

 

We would like to inform you of the following events taking place next week that may affect our operations and service levels.

 

1. ISZE System Unavailability

The ISZE system, managed by Isuzu Japan, will be unavailable from Monday, 10 August 2026 at 15:00h until Tuesday, 11 August 2026 at 17:00h (Belgium time).

As a result, the cut-off time for VOR and Rush orders on Monday, 10 August will be brought forward from the usual 15:00h to 13:00h, enabling us to complete warehouse processing and invoicing before the system becomes unavailable.

Normal operations are expected to resume on Wednesday morning.

Please note that, although the web portal may remain accessible during this period, orders will NOT be transferred to the ISZE system. 

Furthermore, any information displayed may not reflect real-time data and should therefore not be considered fully up to date.

 

2. Isuzu Japan Closure

Isuzu Japan will be closed from 8 August until 16 August 2026.

Consequently, shipments from the supplier may be delayed during this period, and lead times for backordered items may be affected accordingly.

 

3. ISZE Closure on Friday

Please also note that ISZE will be closed on Friday, 14 August 2026, in observance of the Assumption Day holiday on Saturday, 15 August 2026.

 

We understand that these temporary disruptions may create additional challenges for your business, and we sincerely appreciate your patience, flexibility, and understanding during this period. 

Please be assured that our team is closely monitoring the situation and doing everything possible to minimise any impact on your operations and maintain the highest level of service.

Your business is important to us, and we remain committed to supporting you throughout this period. 

Thank you for your continued trust and cooperation.

 

Should you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us.

 

Best regards,

Please find our responses below.

1. CtoC Purchase Orders (to Japan and IMIT)

PO data from ISZE to ISZJ/IMIT will remain on hold while the Control-M jobs are stopped. Once the Control-M jobs resume, the data will be interfaced automatically.

*	IMIT: The PO data will be resent on 12 August at 12:00 PM JST.
*	ISZJ: The PO data will be resent on 13 August at 8:30 AM JST, because the scheduled job on 12 August falls within the Control-M outage period.

The Portal webpage will remain accessible. However, users will not be able to place orders because the RFC connection to SAP S/4HANA will not be available during the outage.

Dear All,

 

Please find our responses below.

1. CtoC Purchase Orders (to Japan and IMIT)

PO data from ISZE to ISZJ/IMIT will remain on hold while the Control-M jobs are stopped. Once the Control-M jobs resume, the data will be interfaced automatically.

*	IMIT: The PO data will be resent on 12 August at 12:00 PM JST.
*	ISZJ: The PO data will be resent on 13 August at 8:30 AM JST, because the scheduled job on 12 August falls within the Control-M outage period.

Therefore, no manual recovery is required.

2. Customer Orders via SAP NetWeaver Portal (NWP)

The Portal webpage will remain accessible. However, users will not be able to place orders because the RFC connection to SAP S/4HANA will not be available during the outage.

As a result, there will be no pending ("stuck") orders, since orders cannot be created during this period. Please inform customers about this.

 

If any, just let us know.

Dear Sebastian Müller san, 

 

Thank you for your message.

 

Immediately after receiving your message, we tested registering data in the system and were able to do so without any issues.

 

It is possible that the error is being caused by a specific portion of the data. Therefore, rather than copying and pasting a large amount of data at once, please try copying and pasting it in smaller portions.

Please also check that you are not attempting to enter data into fields that are not designated as answer fields.

*We also reviewed the Excel file you sent and found that some cells contained data that did not meet the applicable input requirements. 

For example, alphabetical characters were entered in cells that accept numerical values only, and symbols that were not included in the available options were entered in cells requiring a selection from a drop-down list.

Please ensure that the data entered complies with the input requirements specified for each cell. 

Further details regarding these requirements are provided in the User Manual.（Information: Announcement : User Manual 2026 <https://isuzumotorslimited.my.site.com/awards/s/information/a0NRB00001itLLJ2A2/announcement-user-manual-2026> ）

 

If an error occurs, please click the “Revert” button next to the “Save” button to refresh the data, and then try entering and saving the data again.

Additionally, if possible, please log out of the system, close your browser, and then reopen the browser and log in again.

If the issue occurs again, please send us a screenshot of the error. 

When data cannot be registered due to an error, the cell at the far left of the relevant row will be highlighted in red. Please move your cursor over the highlighted cell and take a screenshot that clearly shows the error message displayed.

If the issue still persists after trying the above steps, please contact the Secretariat again.

 

Please note that, regrettably, we are unable to accept the Excel file attached to your previous email as a valid submission.

We kindly ask that you enter your responses directly into the system by 3:00 PM JST today.

If you contact us by 3:00 PM JST today, we can also accept a request for a submission extension (up to 3:00 PM JST on August 6 at the latest). 

However, please be aware that an extension will result in the application of a penalty: if a Star is awarded, the incentive amount will be reduced by 50%.

For further details, please refer to the Response Rulebook distributed on June 5.

 

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

 

Warm regards,

Hi, Duncan,

Thanks for sharing the information.

<Lubricant project>
Regarding the engine oil, IML has initiated the centralised purchasing project since 2023 where they announced it during the CV conference in Yokohama.
The idea is indeed simple - we try to consolidate the volume across the markets and obtain a competitive price from major lubricant manufacturers.
We ask the manufacturers to develop a product equivalent to the Isuzu genuine "Besco" oils. It is not Besco that we would like to promote where we are missing the lubricant sales.
What we would like first of all is to reach a consensus with you to work with some potential dealers if their conditions are met - price, packaging, mode of supply, logistics, ordering, etc.
Secondly, we would like to find out the exact details of these conditions, especially the ordering and logistics, so that we can determine how we can share the profit between ISZE and ITUK (i.e. whether it is built into the price, or loyalty payment). Preferably we would like to visit some target dealers in the coming months.

I have requested Tanaka san's team (IML parts sales group responsible to the project) to give you (and your team) a brief overview to start with (like the attached slides) when you visit them in August.

Dear Balazs,

 

The purpose of this training is to provide distributors with a clear understanding of the Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) solutions and order procedures available at Isuzu Motors Europe.

 

During the session, participants will learn how EDI can automate the exchange of business documents, improve data accuracy, reduce manual processing, and create a more efficient ordering process. The training will also explain the different order types, their intended use, priorities, lead times, and associated procedures, enabling participants to select the most appropriate order type for each situation.

 

By attending this training, distributors will:

*	Gain a solid understanding of the EDI services offered by Isuzu Motors Europe.
*	Learn how to implement and optimize digital order processing.
*	Understand the purpose and correct use of each order type.
*	Reduce ordering errors and unnecessary transportation costs.
*	Improve communication and cooperation with Isuzu Motors Europe.
*	Increase operational efficiency and customer satisfaction through standardized processes.

 

Ultimately, the training is designed to help distributors make better use of Isuzu Motors Europe's digital services, streamline their daily operations, and ensure orders are processed as efficiently and accurately as possible.

Subject: RE: [urgent request] Battery Module P/N 7552125550

 

Dear Peeraya san,

 

Thank you very much for your draft and my apologies for the late reply.

 

Based on the draft, Belgian customs authorities will not approve it as evidence for a Thailand origin claim for the battery pack.
Your draft suggests the shipment contains both Thai origin and Korean origin items, but it does not clarify why the battery pack is considered Thai origin.

For customs purposes I would like to ask following question to you :
Can you confirm that the Thai Chamber of Commerce will issue the CoO showing the complete high voltage battery assembly as being of Thailand origin, rather than the goods were only exported from Thailand?
In my view making the distinction between ‘Thai origin’ and ‘exported from Thailand’ is very crucial in case of an audit.


If Belgian customs authorities audit this in 3 years time it is important that ISZE can show the following :

*	Official Thai CoO
*	Reference to the manufacturer (IMCT) with the emphasis on the ‘substantial transformation’
*	Manufacturing flow description (to strengthen the substantial transformation)
*	Cost/added-value breakdown

 

By providing this, the Thai origin becomes much more defensible.

Without filing the above, customs authorities can still argue that the Korean modules determine the origin (aka the essential character) of the battery pack.

 

Step one : contacting Thai chamber of commerce to obtain the CoO of the battery pack

Step two : file all necessary documentation to prove the substantial transformation in TH to obtain Thai origin.

 

Don’t hesitate contacting me in case of further questions.

 

Met vriendelijke groeten/Best regards

Hello Nuno,

first of all, sorry with this late follow up mail after the conference.



 

1.	Regarding campaigns: At the moment we would prefer working with an SPA (=Special price agreement) instead of a campaign.
	As we have a new pricing policy, we currently see more possibilities in getting an SPA internal approved as we should have than a commitment from the distributor.
	Advantage is we can work with a tailor-made list for parts where I motors notice they lose sales which is leaking to the aftermarket.
	Can you please advise which parts you would like to have on the list. I added a file which you can fill in. For our management the bare minimum is that the turnover for ISZE would increase this you can check by yourself in the file.
2.	I added a complete fresh price with fig key indication in the end. In a second file you have the description of the fig key.
	Please let us know if you have any questions / need assistance.
3.	Could we have an update of how R&M is going for both CV & LCV? Do you require any assistance from ISZE?
4.	Regarding EDI connection my colleague Bart has sent out or will soon send out an email for a training regarding EDI.
	After the training we can formally set up the connection between our systems.
5.	I also added the BVP parts catalogue as a conversion file where you can see the genuine counterpart
6.	Please see attached the IDS file, I also created a tool to compare DLR performances, it’s the HTML file (works offline)
	Do you already have any idea for a potential Isuzu dealer standard visit after the summer?
	
	

During our meeting at the conference Masumi san was explaining about a GPS =(Genuine parts share) target and we would like to set a separate meeting for this topic.
We can add other topics as well of course. Do you have time for a meeting somewhere next week? Would be good if Luis could join as it’s basically regarding an extended target.

subject: [FYI important] Update EUDR-regulation
body_preview:
Dear All,

 

The EU did a proposal to remove commodities from the Annex I (and also add commodities, but there is no impact for the ISZ-group).

 

Commodities completely removed from the EUDR-scope :

HS 4010: Conveyor belts and transmission belts of vulcanized rubber.

HS 4016: Other articles of vulcanized rubber (e.g., rubber gaskets, seals, or mats).

HS 4101: Raw hides and skins of bovine or equine animals.

HS 4104: Tanned or crust hides and skins of bovine or equine animals, without hair.

HS 4107: Leather further prepared after tanning or crusting (including leather used for car or airplane seats).


Commodities narrowed down from the EUDR-scope :

HS 1201 --> HS 1201 90 00: The scope for soybeans has been restricted. Soya beans intended for sowing (seeds) are now officially exempt.

HS 4012 --> HS ex 4012 90 30: Retreaded or used tires are largely exempt. Only new rubber interchangeable tire treads used for retreading remain in scope; the used tire casing itself is exempt.

HS 9401 --> HS ex 9401: The scope for seats has been strictly limited to wooden seats and wooden parts of seats. Seats upholstered with leather (such as aircraft, automotive, or cinema seats) are now definitively exempt.

HS 9406 10 00 --> HS ex 9406 10 00: The scope for prefabricated buildings has been restricted. Used and second-hand wooden buildings (such as a relocated pre-owned cabin or temporary shed) are now exempt.

 

The exemption takes effect immediately once de Delegated Act passes its formal scrutiny period (2 months).

This means the EU Parliament and Council have the time to raise objections until mid Sept 2026.

If no objections are raised, these products are officially dropped from the requirements (after publication in the official EU-journal) before the EUDR Compliance deadline (30.12.2026) kicks in.

This means we, as an EU-importer do not have to prepare a DDS.

 

Key objectives of the amendment are :

*	Reduce unnecessary administrative (compliance) burden : removing products with a limited link to deforestation or where compliance costs are considered disproportionate
*	Close regulatory gaps : adding certain processed products that were intentionally omitted from Annex I
*	Increase legal certainty : refining tariff codes coverage

 

What does this mean for our ISZ-group-business?
The amendments are favourable as several automotive-related products have been removed from the EUDR-scope.

This means ISZE is ‘out of scope’ after a screening of our master data.


All ISZE-stakeholders (ISZJ, IMIT, IAST) are informed in the meantime.

 

Why is adoption of this delegated act highly likely, after the 2 months scrutiny period (mid Sept 2026) ?

*	the amendments simplify EUDR rather than tighten it
*	the Commission explains why certain products have little reference to deforestation risk
*	following the one-year postponement (30.12.2025) there has been a broad political support for reducing unnecessary compliance costs

 

Don’t hesitate to contact me in case of further questions,

 

Met vriendelijke groeten/Best regards

	Dear Jimmy,
	 
	As discussed, we understand that the cancellation of the inbound order and the PO should technically be sufficient to make it possible for SAP too accept the Valuation type box to be completed.
	However, there are some other concerns that should be taken into account when we need to “re-create” the PO and process the ASN for the receiving of these modules at NISSIN warehouse.
	 
	Because we cannot recreate the same PO number and because it is a CtoC PO, when this new PO is interfaced to IMIT,  they will recognise this as a new requirement and send us new parts. 
	It will be too confusing and too much additional work for everyone that the risk of something going wrong in that process is too high.
	 

		*	My proposal is that we create a standard order (starting with 451*) for this part.

	IMIT has issued an invoice linked to the current CtoC PO (0072600102), which we will also need to delete from SAP in order to fix the master data. 
	Because IMIT will not receive this new PO, they will also not issue an ASN or an invoice but they do expect to be paid for the parts they have shipped on the existing invoice.
	The existing ASN will need to be deleted and new ASN will have to be created linked to this new standard PO.

נושא: Delays in order processing for regular SEA orders

 

Dear all,

 

I wanted to flag something that is affecting our shipments right now. We have seen a real increase in customs checks on our end. These inspections can be both administrative and physical.

 

The physical inspections can take up to a month to clear. Luckily, we have had only one so far: invoice 202741824. The same delay also applies to invoices 202741818 through 202741823 since these belong together in the same container. We have not yet received a date for this inspection from customs, so we have also not been able to book a new pickup with Nippon.

 

We currently have 3 shipments stuck in a customs process. As a direct consequence, we have not been able to start picking SOR orders since last week (PO reference UTI 2614897, PO reference 2615054). Normal operations are on hold until the first shipment can leave, which is now planned for 22 July, port conditions permitting.

 

Next week, on 22 July, a container with invoices 202741454 to 202741457 is set to depart, and hopefully soon after that another one with invoices 202742326 and 202742328 as well. All documents for both shipments have been released, so we do not expect customs delay on those.

 

We are doing what we can to speed things up, but honestly, the timeline is in customs' hands, not ours. We will keep you posted as soon as there is movement.

Please let us know if you have any questions. But if you require parts urgent, we recommend to order them via AIR.

 

Thank you for understanding.


Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst

subject: Delays in order processing for regular SEA orders
body_preview:
Dear all,



 

I wanted to flag something that is affecting our shipments right now. We have seen a real increase in customs checks on our end. These inspections can be both administrative and physical.

 

The physical inspections can take up to a month to clear. Luckily, we have had only one so far: invoice 202741824. The same delay also applies to invoices 202741818 through 202741823 since these belong together in the same container. We have not yet received a date for this inspection from customs, so we have also not been able to book a new pickup with Nippon.

 

We currently have 3 shipments stuck in a customs process. As a direct consequence, we have not been able to start picking SOR orders since last week (PO reference UTI 2614897, PO reference 2615054). Normal operations are on hold until the first shipment can leave, which is now planned for 22 July, port conditions permitting.

 

Next week, on 22 July, a container with invoices 202741454 to 202741457 is set to depart, and hopefully soon after that another one with invoices 202742326 and 202742328 as well. All documents for both shipments have been released, so we do not expect customs delay on those.

 

We are doing what we can to speed things up, but honestly, the timeline is in customs' hands, not ours. We will keep you posted as soon as there is movement.

Please let us know if you have any questions. But if you require parts urgent, we recommend to order them via AIR.

 

Thank you for understanding.


Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

	The current UIO file treats all N-Series CV LD units (2,206) as one undifferentiated bucket, priced at a single GPS rate of €739/unit/yr.

body_preview:
Dear Jimmy,

 

As discussed, we understand that the cancellation of the inbound order and the PO should technically be sufficient to make it possible for SAP too accept the Valuation type box to be completed.

However, there are some other concerns that should be taken into account when we need to “re-create” the PO and process the ASN for the receiving of these modules at NISSIN warehouse.

 

Because we cannot recreate the same PO number and because it is a CtoC PO, when this new PO is interfaced to IMIT,  they will recognise this as a new requirement and send us new parts. 

It will be too confusing and too much additional work for everyone that the risk of something going wrong in that process is too high.

 

	*	My proposal is that we create a standard order (starting with 451*) for this part.

This standard PO is not interfaced with IMIT to avoid confusion on their side and reduce the risk of a new shipment. 

 

This standard PO should work in theory, but I do have some concerns related to the ASN and invoice processing. 
IMIT has issued an invoice linked to the current CtoC PO (0072600102), which we will also need to delete from SAP in order to fix the master data. 
Because IMIT will not receive this new PO, they will also not issue an ASN or an invoice but they do expect to be paid for the parts they have shipped on the existing invoice.

The existing ASN will need to be deleted and new ASN will have to be created linked to this new standard PO.

 

	*	Can the ASN be created by GS to match the invoice from IMIT with the standard PO information?
	*	How will this affect the booking of this invoice on accounting side?
	*	The PO on the PDF invoice will also not match with the PO in the ASN, will this cause any issues?
	*	When IMIT receives payment for a PO number that is not recognised, how does that work?

 

Thank you in advance for checking.

 

 

Best Regards,

I hope you are doing well.

 

Following the discussions between Allianz and Isuzu Motors Europe towards the end of last year, I wanted to reach out to reconnect.

 

We are pleased to see that the cooperation with Isuzu Portugal is now starting, and we look forward to following its progress. During our previous conversations, you mentioned that you would provide us with more detailed information about Allianz Europe's capabilities and organization.

 

From Isuzu Motors Europe's perspective, the interest in exploring a broader European rollout is now very concrete. We believe there are opportunities to build on the local success and assess how a European partnership could create value for both organizations.

 

We would therefore welcome the opportunity to continue our discussions, explore the available possibilities in more detail, and discuss how we could introduce Allianz to our European distributor network.

 

Please let us know your availability for a meeting in the coming weeks. We look forward to continuing the conversation.

Thank you very much for your update and for checking the Shell product pricing for UMI.

I looked into the matter and checked the relevant market prices.
Based on our review, the competitive market level for similar Shell products is around €2.2 per liter.

Unfortunately, even the price offered before the upcoming price increase is still too high. 
Therefore, we will not be able to proceed with the order at this stage, as it would not allow us to be competitive in the Israeli market.

If there is any flexibility to significantly improve the price, closer to around €2 per liter, we would be happy to review the opportunity again.

I believe that with the right pricing, this could create a win-win opportunity for both sides.

Thank you again for your support and cooperation.

Dear Saskia,

 

Apologies that the investigation from the IML side took some time.

For this CR, the current budgetary estimate is expected to be below JPY 1,000,000, approximately EUR 5K.

Please note that this amount is provided for budgeting purposes only. A formal quotation will be provided later, once the implementation timing and detailed requirements have been confirmed.

If you need this CR to be implemented, I think there are two options:

1.	The requirement is not urgent and can wait for the next FY2028 budget and CR plan.
2.	The requirement needs to be implemented in the current FY2027. This means that additional budget approval will be required, and the earliest schedule to start the implementation would be after the SAP version-up, let’s say from January 2027.

 

Please let us know how you would like to proceed.

 

Best regards,
Jimmy

Dear Suzuki san,

FYI regarding ITUK :

Parts Sales: MTD Parts sales for May finished at £1,241,343 vs an original plan of £1,059,183, ahead of plan by £182,160. 

*	Promotions: Our suspension promotion launched in June and will run through to end of July. The previous clutch promotion did not perform well and delivered average results.
*	FY26\27 Year-on-Year Comparison: Our daily run rate for FY26/27 has increased by 8.76% compared to FY25/26, this is down from a from last month.
*	Stock Availability & MOS: Stock levels maintained at our planned levels, however extra sales effort is required to meet the ISZE target and rebate by end of year. MOS is slightly up from 4.59 to 4.62 for May. Our first pick rate is currently at 94.51%, this down against our target of 95%. TVS again had multiple lean lifts down during June which effected the first pick rate.
*	MDI, E-Commerce & GSCM: The MDI Project has moved to TVS to quote & scope, with their 1st quote higher than expected. DY is negotiating the price to see if it can be brought down. E-Commerce PoC is now with RH Commercials, Allports & Ferndown to trial, however not much progress in June due to DY’s other commitments during June. GSCM is currently in POC phase. Weekly meetings in place to make sure projects stay on track. 
*	Regional Growth: Regional growth up in June across all regions except the South East, Tony Black’s 1st month has gone well with most dealers already been visited as a 1st introduction.

Subject: Security parts supply management

 

Dear Hadi,

 

We have a new (new to us…) requirement for managing the supply of security parts, under the EU’s Repair and Maintenance Information (RMI) regulation.

Under the regulation, the economic operator must conduct the customer verification, and keep the record of the sales.

 

Can we sit down together and discuss what/how we can do this?

 

What I understood is that we need build in the verification process, and the record-keeping system.

How to get the verification is via the agency called SERMI.

 

My guess is that we need to get this information from the distributor, along with the VIN, when they order the key.

 

We need to establish such a structure before the end of the year. Otherwise, the worst case is that we cannot get the type approval for any of our vehicles sold in the EU market.

 

 

Since we have not much time as some of you are receiving visitors and travelling for business this week,

I asked Copilot and got the following response:

 

Under EU Regulation 2018/858 and its Delegated Regulation 2021/1244, access to security-related vehicle parts and information is tightly controlled to balance repair market competition with vehicle cybersecurity. Here's a detailed breakdown:

 

🔐 What Are Security-Related Parts?

Security-related parts and functions include:

 

Anti-theft systems

Electronic immobilizers

Alarm systems

Remote keyless entry

Vehicle access control modules

Software and diagnostics related to these systems

These components are critical to preventing unauthorized access or theft, and therefore require controlled access for repair and maintenance.

 

🛠️ How Is Access Controlled?

1. SERMI Scheme (Security-Related RMI)

The SERMI (Security-related Repair and Maintenance Information) system is the EU-wide framework for managing access to security-related vehicle data

body_preview:
Dear Suzuki san,

Please see below background & justification for both UTI & IUK. We have an ambitious target and want to achieve it together with the DB’s.



This SPA covers 48 competitive part lines over a 12-month period for UTI Israel.

The requested SPA scenario represents a total revenue commitment of €1,041,022, compared with an L12 baseline of €733,689. This equals a revenue uplift of €307,333 / +41.9%, driven by a committed volume increase from 17,184 pcs to 27,692 pcs.

Gross margin reduces from 41.7% under the L12 baseline to 29.6% under the SPA scenario. No IML/IMIT purchase price support is requested; ISZE absorbs the full margin-rate reduction. Despite the lower margin percentage, absolute gross profit improves from €306,296 to €307,853, resulting in a positive profit impact of +€1,557.

Market Context
UTI is facing strong aftermarket competition in Israel across these selected part lines. These are not brake-only parts; they are competitive items where UTI is losing genuine parts sales to IAM brands, local aftermarket suppliers, and parallel import channels.

Parallel import remains a major issue in the Israeli market and continues to create direct price pressure against genuine ISUZU parts. The objective of this SPA is to recover and defend genuine parts volume before these sales are permanently absorbed by non-genuine channels.

SPA Mechanics

Price relief is linked to binding volume commitments. UTI receives the SPA price only against the agreed committed quantities.
A mid-period review should be included. If UTI achieves less than 80% of the committed run-rate, ISZE reserves the right to revert to standard pricing without penalty.
There is no automatic rollover. Any continuation after the SPA period requires separate review and re-approval.

Approval Rationale

The objective is to defend genuine ISUZU parts volume in Israel against IAM competition and parallel import. SPA pricing is conditional on committed volume and is justified only where it protects or recovers genuine parts sales that are otherwise at risk of being lost to non-genuine channels.

Approval is recommended because the proposal delivers significant volume and revenue recovery while maintaining a positive absolute gross profit impact, without requesting additional IML/IMIT purchase price support.

 		
		
		
		


Purpose & background of IUK:




Special Pricing Agreement — Isuzu Truck UK (IUK)  |  Market: United Kingdom

This SPA covers 30 brake part lines over a 6-month period (mid-May to mid-November 2026). Total SPA revenue commitment: €289,477 vs L6 baseline of €217,902 — a +32.8% volume-driven uplift (+1,742 units committed over 6 months).
Gross margin moves from 50.9% (L6) to 41.0% (SPA). No IML/IMIT purchase price support is requested — ISZE absorbs the full margin rate reduction. The absolute gross profit improvement is +€7,649 (from €110,953 to €118,601), driven entirely by committed volume uplift.

MARKET CONTEXT:
IUK fleet in operation (UIO): 47,783 pickups (May 2026), declining to 44,923 by end-2026 as the UK  fleet ages under ZEV mandate pressure. This window of peak brake parts demand on the current fleet must be maximised now. IAM competitors  are undercutting ISZE genuine prices. 

SPA MECHANICS:
Price relief is linked to binding volume commitments. IUK only receives the SPA price if committed quantities are met. A 3-month interim review is built in: if IUK achieves less than 80% of committed volume by mid-August 2026, ISZE reserves the right to revert to standard pricing without penalty. No automatic rollover — re-approval required after 6 months.


Objective: defend genuine parts volume against IAM price competition. SPA pricing is conditional on volume commitments.

 		
		
		
		





Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst

The Parts Division is currently going through several changes, and a new team member, Netanel, has recently joined us.
He will be managing the full Isuzu operation, and I have copied him to this email.

Regarding UMI sales to dealers, the current figure stands at approximately - 190,016 EUR

There was no special campaign or dedicated activity this month this is part of our regular ongoing business.

Regarding the oil business, we would be happy to discuss possible ideas and joint activities that will help maintain and strengthen the purchasing activity with Isuzu.

This is an important topic for us, both from an inventory and operational perspective, and also as part of our mutual interest in preserving and developing the business relationship between UMI and Isuzu. We would be happy to explore together how we can move this forward.

subject: EUBR update
body_preview:
Good morning, all.

Can you please follow up on the survey related to the battery collection, scrapping and recycling in the European countries?
There are a several countries where we have no information. While the distributors in these countries are yet to order RG20/30, it is high time we obtain the relevant information.

As well as the general situations, we have some specific questions that IML's working group would like to clarify:

1.	
	Iceland: According to their own survey through a consultancy firm, an organisation called IRF is the only PRO in Iceland.
	Can you confirm whether this is indeed the case?
	If so, can you confirm whether BL is registered to (or has a contract with) IRF for battery collection/scrapping/recycling with certain fees?
2.	
	UK: Again, according to their own survey, under the UK regulations, the management of the waste batteries (collection, treatment, recycling and export) must be handled by an approved battery treatment operator (ABTO).
	IUK's Car Take Back does not appear to be ab ABTO. Can you confirm whether Car Take Back delivers collected batteries to a certain ABTO?


In addition, our current understanding about the PRO and ERP in each country that ISZE will need to act as PRO in Belgium, we need to accelerate implementing the regulations compliance structure, as IBX has started ordering several units (see below the latest production order results).
Can you please follow up with Reneos quotation? 



Can you please provide me with updates by Friday this week - 3 July?

Thanks,

Masumi

body_preview:
Beste collega’s,

We hebben leuk nieuws om met jullie te delen!

Via onze samenwerking met Pluxee krijgen jullie vanaf nu toegang tot Benefits at Work: een uitgebreid voordelenplatform boordevol exclusieve kortingen, interessante deals en voordelige tickets.

Of je nu graag shopt, een dagje uit plant, naar de cinema gaat of gewoon wil besparen op je favoriete merken — er zit voor iedereen wel iets tussen! 😊

Wat mag je verwachten?

✨ Kortingen bij bekende winkels en webshops
🎬 Voordelige cinema- en pretparktickets
✈️ Deals voor reizen en uitstappen
👟 Voordelen op mode, sport, technologie en lifestyle
🍴 Aanbiedingen voor restaurants en vrije tijd
… en nog veel meer!

Het aanbod wordt regelmatig vernieuwd, dus het loont zeker de moeite om af en toe eens een kijkje te nemen.

________________________________

Hoe kan je je aanmelden?

1.Ga naar https://isuzu.benefitsatwork.be

 

2. Klik op ‘nu registreren’.

 

3. Maak een account aan met je persoonlijk e-mailadres en de registratiecode: Isuzu@Benefits!

 

4. Vink aan dat je de maandelijkse nieuwsbrief wilt ontvangen om op de hoogte te blijven van nieuwe aangesloten merken en aanbiedingen.

 

5. Check je inbox voor de activeringscode. Vul deze code in bij ‘account activeren’.

 

________________________________

Heb je vragen of lukt de registratie niet meteen? Neem gerust contact op met HR.

Veel plezier met het ontdekken van alle voordelen! 🎁

________________________________

________________________________

Dear colleagues,

We have some exciting news to share with you!

Through our partnership with Pluxee, you now have access to Benefits at Work: a comprehensive benefits platform packed with exclusive discounts, great deals, and discounted tickets.

Whether you enjoy shopping, planning a day out, going to the movies, or simply saving money on your favorite brands — there’s something for everyone! 😊

What can you expect?

✨ Discounts at popular stores and online shops
🎬 Reduced-price cinema and theme park tickets
✈️ Special offers on travel and leisure activities
👟 Benefits on fashion, sports, technology, and lifestyle products
🍴 Discounts for restaurants and entertainment
…and much more!

The offers are updated regularly, so it’s definitely worth checking the platform from time to time.

________________________________

How do you register?

1. Go to: https://isuzu.benefitsatwork.be <https://isuzu.benefitsatwork.be> 

2. Click on "Register Now".

3. Create an account using your personal email address and the registration code: Isuzu@Benefits!

4. Tick the box to subscribe to the monthly newsletter so you can stay informed about newly added brands and special offers.

5. Check your inbox for the activation code and enter it under "Activate Account".

________________________________

If you have any questions or experience any issues during registration, please feel free to contact HR.

Enjoy exploring all the benefits! 🎁

Kind regards

body_preview:
Dear Saskia,

Apologies that the investigation from the IML side took some time.
For this CR, the current budgetary estimate is expected to be below JPY 1,000,000, approximately EUR 5K.
Please note that this amount is provided for budgeting purposes only. A formal quotation will be provided later, once the implementation timing and detailed requirements have been confirmed.
If you need this CR to be implemented, I think there are two options:

1.	The requirement is not urgent and can wait for the next FY2028 budget and CR plan.
2.	The requirement needs to be implemented in the current FY2027. This means that additional budget approval will be required, and the earliest schedule to start the implementation would be after the SAP version-up, let’s say from January 2027.


Please let us know how you would like to proceed.

Best regards,
Jimmy

		We need to get the necessary information from the distributor, along with the VIN, when they order a key.
		We need to establish such a structure before the end of the year.

subject: A Gift from Isuzu: A Day Off on Your Birthday! 🎉
body_preview:
Dear colleagues,

Beste collega's,

 

We have some great news!

We hebben leuk nieuws!

As an additional benefit, all colleagues will receive an extra vacation day on their birthday this year. This arrangement applies to birthdays occurring between July 2026 and June 2027.

Als extra voordeel krijgen alle collega's dit jaar een extra vakantiedag op hun verjaardag. Deze regeling geldt voor verjaardagen in de periode van juli 2026 tot en met juni 2027.

 

________________________________

How does it work?

Hoe werkt het?

 

Are you celebrating your birthday on a regular working day?

Your birthday leave will automatically be scheduled in Yeap, so that you can enjoy your special day without any worries.

Ben je jarig op een gewone werkdag?
Dan wordt je verjaardagsverlof automatisch voor jou ingepland in Yeap, zodat je zorgeloos van je speciale dag kunt genieten.

 

Are you celebrating your birthday on a weekend, public holiday, or your regular day off?

In that case, you may take this extra leave day during the same week as your birthday or in the following week. We ask you to coordinate this with your manager in advance and inform HR of the chosen date. Once HR has been notified, the leave day will be registered in Yeap.

Ben je jarig in het weekend, op een feestdag of op je vaste vrije dag?
Dan mag je deze extra verlofdag opnemen in dezelfde week als je verjaardag of in de week erna. We vragen je om hierover vooraf af te stemmen met je manager en de gekozen dag door te geven aan HR. Zodra HR hiervan op de hoogte is, wordt de verlofdag in Yeap geregistreerd.

A small request for flexibility

Sometimes a birthday coincides with an important business trip, customer appointment, or crucial meeting. In such situations, we ask for flexibility in working together with your manager to determine a suitable date for taking this extra leave day.

Een kleine vraag om flexibiliteit

Soms valt een verjaardag samen met een belangrijke business trip, klantafspraak of cruciale meeting. In dergelijke situaties vragen we flexibiliteit om samen met de manager een passend moment voor deze extra verlofdag te bepalen.

 

________________________________

 

We hope this extra day contributes to a wonderful birthday! Consider it a well-deserved opportunity to take a break, take some time for yourself, or simply enjoy something you would not normally have the chance to do.

We hopen dat deze extra dag bijdraagt aan een fijne verjaardag ! Zie het als een welverdiend moment om even op adem te komen, tijd te maken voor jezelf of gewoon te genieten van iets waar je anders niet aan toekomt. 

We would also like to thank you for your dedication, flexibility, and commitment — day after day. We recognize that a lot is often asked of you, and that you continue to contribute to our organization with the same level of enthusiasm and professionalism. We truly appreciate your efforts.

We willen jullie graag bedanken voor jullie inzet, flexibiliteit en betrokkenheid — elke dag opnieuw. We merken dat er vaak veel gevraagd wordt en dat jullie telkens met dezelfde toewijding blijven bijdragen aan onze organisatie. Dat waarderen we enorm.

Wishing a very happy birthday in advance to everyone celebrating their birthday in the coming months! 🎂

Alvast een gelukkige verjaardag toegewenst aan iedereen die de komende maanden een jaartje wijzer wordt! 🎂

 

Kind regards

Subject: ISA案件に関する事前共有（CV Conference / After-sales Meeting） 

 

吉本さん、早川さん、

 

いつもお世話になっております。

来週開催予定のCV Conference / After-sales Meetingに先立ち、本件に関する現状および今後の対応について共有させていただきます。

 

【1. 来週の会議について】
IMIT部品部からは、Sales Group GLのKawinおよび欧州担当のPeeryaの2名が参加予定です。

また、カンファレンス期間中に個別ミーティングを予定しております。（下段をご参照ください）

ISAとの打合せについては、サービス部主導で実施予定であり、部品部も同席いたします。

会議では、ISA向け回答レターに記載した内容に沿って、現時点でのステータスをご説明する予定です。

 

【2. 確認事項】
弊部スタッフ（山居も同席）からの報告ですが、昨日のISZE-IMIT間の隔週会議において本件を取り上げた際、ISZE部品部（営業グループ）内での認識が十分に共有されていないように見受けられました。

当方の認識違いであれば恐縮ですが、ISAとの今後のコミュニケーションを円滑に進めるためにも、改めて関係者間でご確認いただけますと幸いです。

 

【3. お願い事項】
本件を受けて、MY26モデルに関するISAからのオーダー対応状況については、ISZE部品部担当よりISA部品担当へ適宜進捗共有が行われるよう、ご確認をお願いいたします。

ISAとの窓口はISZEになりますので、本件についてもISAとの継続的な情報共有およびフォローアップをお願いいたします。

また、来週予定しておりますISAとの個別会議につきまして、昨日の隔週会議では他社との個別会議との兼ね合いもありISZE側の参加可否は未定と伺っておりますが、可能であればどなたかご同席いただけますと幸いです。

 

【4. その他の情報共有】
ISAのBranding DirectorであるPerさんより、IMIEおよびIMIT車両営業経由でBEVアフターセールス関連の進捗について問い合わせを受けております。

来週のISAとの打合せにおいて、BEVアフターセールス関連の現状進捗について説明を行う予定ですので、その旨を車両営業経由で回答済みです。

また、今回のカンファレンスには、出席者リストによるとISAよりAfter-sales DirectorのNiklasさん、およびParts & Logistics ManagerのLouiseさんも参加予定と伺っております。もし機会がございましたら、ご挨拶いただければ幸いです。

 

なお、BEV新車からのバッテリーパック交換（SWAP）が実施できない件につきましては、IMITサービス部よりIMCTサービス部を通じて開発へ見解および対応方針の確認を依頼しているとのことです。新たな情報が入り次第、共有させていただきます。

 

【5. 今後について】
IMIT・ISZE・欧州DB間における業務フロー見直し案につきましては、来週のカンファレンス終了後に改めて協議の場を設定させていただく予定です。

以上、来週の会議に向けた事前共有となります。

 

引き続きよろしくお願いいたし

また、カンファレンス期間中に個別ミーティングを予定しております。（下段をご参照ください）

ISAとの打合せについては、サービス部主導で実施予定であり、部品部も同席いたします。

会議では、ISA向け回答レターに記載した内容に沿って、現時点でのステータスをご説明する予定です。

 

【2. 確認事項】
弊部スタッフ（山居も同席）からの報告ですが、昨日のISZE-IMIT間の隔週会議において本件を取り上げた際、ISZE部品部（営業グループ）内での認識が十分に共有されていないように見受けられました。

当方の認識違いであれば恐縮ですが、ISAとの今後のコミュニケーションを円滑に進めるためにも、改めて関係者間でご確認いただけますと幸いです。

 

【3. お願い事項】
本件を受けて、MY26モデルに関するISAからのオーダー対応状況については、ISZE部品部担当よりISA部品担当へ適宜進捗共有が行われるよう、ご確認をお願いいたします。

ISAとの窓口はISZEになりますので、本件についてもISAとの継続的な情報共有およびフォローアップをお願いいたします。

また、来週予定しておりますISAとの個別会議につきまして、昨日の隔週会議では他社との個別会議との兼ね合いもありISZE側の参加可否は未定と伺っておりますが、可能であればどなたかご同席いただけますと幸いです。

 

【4. その他の情報共有】
ISAのBranding DirectorであるPerさんより、IMIEおよびIMIT車両営業経由でBEVアフターセールス関連の進捗について問い合わせを受けております。

来週のISAとの打合せにおいて、BEVアフターセールス関連の現状進捗について説明を行う予定ですので、その旨を車両営業経由で回答済みです。

また、今回のカンファレンスには、出席者リストによるとISAよりAfter-sales DirectorのNiklasさん、およびParts & Logistics ManagerのLouiseさんも参加予定と伺っております。もし機会がございましたら、ご挨拶いただければ幸いです。

 

なお、BEV新車からのバッテリーパック交換（SWAP）が実施できない件につきましては、IMITサービス部よりIMCTサービス部を通じて開発へ見解および対応方針の確認を依頼しているとのことです。新たな情報が入り次第、共有させていただきます。

 

【5. 今後について】
IMIT・ISZE・欧州DB間における業務フロー見直し案につきましては、来週のカンファレンス終了後に改めて協議の場を設定させていただく予定です。

以上、来週の会議に向けた事前共有となります。

subject: Evaluation cycle – update on compensation and benefits
body_preview:
Dear colleagues,

 

As every year, we have started the evaluation cycle.

 

We would like to communicate transparently about its impact on compensation. Due to the current salary freeze imposed by the government, it is unfortunately not possible this year to grant general gross salary increases. One exception applies: employees who receive a promotion as part of this evaluation cycle will be eligible for an adjusted salary.

 

We understand that this may be disappointing for many of you. Therefore, together with our directors, we are exploring which alternative benefits we can offer to continue showing our appreciation. As soon as concrete decisions are taken, we will of course inform you.

 

What we can already confirm today:

*	Meal vouchers will be increased from €8 to €10
*	The teleworking allowance will be increased with 50 EUR (pro rate for part-time employees)

 

These measures are part of a broader approach in which the budget for salary increases is being redirected towards other benefits, within the applicable legal framework.

 

We remain committed to handling this in a fair and transparent way.

 

If you have any questions or would like to discuss this further, please do not hesitate to contact me.

 

Kind regards,

Els Smedts

Dear Peeraya san,

 

Thank you very much for your draft and my apologies for the late reply.

 

Based on the draft, Belgian customs authorities will not approve it as evidence for a Thailand origin claim for the battery pack.
Your draft suggests the shipment contains both Thai origin and Korean origin items, but it does not clarify why the battery pack is considered Thai origin.

For customs purposes I would like to ask following question to you :
Can you confirm that the Thai Chamber of Commerce will issue the CoO showing the complete high voltage battery assembly as being of Thailand origin, rather than the goods were only exported from Thailand?
In my view making the distinction between ‘Thai origin’ and ‘exported from Thailand’ is very crucial in case of an audit.


If Belgian customs authorities audit this in 3 years time it is important that ISZE can show the following :

*	Official Thai CoO
*	Reference to the manufacturer (IMCT) with the emphasis on the ‘substantial transformation’ 
*	Manufacturing flow description (to strengthen the substantial transformation)
*	Cost/added-value breakdown

 

By providing this, the Thai origin becomes much more defensible.

Without filing the above, customs authorities can still argue that the Korean modules determine the origin (aka the essential character) of the battery pack.

 

Step one : contacting Thai chamber of commerce to obtain the CoO of the battery pack

Step two : file all necessary documentation to prove the substantial transformation in TH to obtain Thai origin.

 

Don’t hesitate contacting me in case of further questions.

 

Met vriendelijke groeten/Best regards

subject: Genuine parts share
body_preview:
Dear all,

I hope you are fine

First, some background on what ISZE is building  ( based on Isuzu MTBP), since the term may be new to you. We track something internally called Genuine Parts Share (GPS). The idea is simple: for a given vehicle population, a certain number of parts should be consumed over time, through normal servicing, wear, and repairs. GPS measures how much of that expected demand is actually captured by genuine Isuzu parts versus what leaks to the independent aftermarket (IAM). A low GPS on a part means we're losing that business to non-genuine suppliers.

 

To build a credible model I need to separate the different channels through which a genuine part gets consumed. Warranty repairs are one of those channels, and right now ISZE can't see them for UMI.
Warranty-fitted parts don't show up in distributor sell-out, so without your data I'd be undercounting genuine consumption and the GPS picture for UMI would be distorted.
We already received the data from IMG for the other DB’s.

 

What I'm after specifically:

 

- Warranty parts consumption for the UMI market, by part number

- Quantity used per part number (units), ideally over the last 3 full years

 

I don't need claim detail, cost, or VINs — just the part numbers and the quantities fitted under warranty.

This would help us tremendously.

Man thanks in advance and kind regards,

 

Jérôme Van der Pluym

body_preview:
Dear Jerome,

This is a very good question.

As you can see on the report, you have sales, Cost of Sales (COS), Gross Profit (GP) and GP (excl. Provisions).


Within COS, you have COS variances too.  Which means, this is not the cost of your material/product or MAP (purchase price+freight in+other logistic costs), but also storage costs-freight out-duties-... and provisions stock changes (depreciation costs inventory).



 

As you can see, the depreciation cost of scrapping is very high this month due to the increase of interchangeable C materials.  

 

BVdB has already double checked if this was correct and was confirmed.

This was also one of the reasons why we asked to take attention on the depreciated materials (see attached e-mails).

Hope this is an answer on your question.  If something is not clear or you want some further explanation, I’m happy to do so.

Best regards,

 

Giuna

body_preview:
Dear Peeraya san,

 

Thank you very much for your draft and my apologies for the late reply.

 

Based on the draft, Belgian customs authorities will not approve it as evidence for a Thailand origin claim for the battery pack.
Your draft suggests the shipment contains both Thai origin and Korean origin items, but it does not clarify why the battery pack is considered Thai origin.

For customs purposes I would like to ask following question to you :
Can you confirm that the Thai Chamber of Commerce will issue the CoO showing the complete high voltage battery assembly as being of Thailand origin, rather than the goods were only exported from Thailand?
In my view making the distinction between ‘Thai origin’ and ‘exported from Thailand’ is very crucial in case of an audit.


If Belgian customs authorities audit this in 3 years time it is important that ISZE can show the following :

*	Official Thai CoO
*	Reference to the manufacturer (IMCT) with the emphasis on the ‘substantial transformation’ 
*	Manufacturing flow description (to strengthen the substantial transformation)
*	Cost/added-value breakdown

 

By providing this, the Thai origin becomes much more defensible.

Without filing the above, customs authorities can still argue that the Korean modules determine the origin (aka the essential character) of the battery pack.

 

Step one : contacting Thai chamber of commerce to obtain the CoO of the battery pack

Step two : file all necessary documentation to prove the substantial transformation in TH to obtain Thai origin.

 

Don’t hesitate contacting me in case of further questions.

 

Met vriendelijke groeten/Best regards

Sorry for not coming back to you earlier as I was procrastinating over how to show the figures. I kind of wanted to make the original plan visible, so that we know how much progress we made, and how much more we still need to make.

Dear Bart san,

 

Thank you for your explanation and sorry for the delayed response from IMIT.

We understand that ISA placed the initial order without prior notice to ISZE, after which the backorder situation occurred.

At the same time, based on the information received so far, we understand that the order volume from ISA may have exceeded the original forecast and contributed to the backorder situation. 

Therefore, Yoshimoto-san, Hayakawa-san, Ogashiwa-san and I discussed this matter and agreed that it would be helpful to evaluate whether ISA's order should be regarded as a normal order within the expected range or as an exceptional/high-volume order.

Could you please review this point and share ISZE's assessment with us when available?

 

On the other hand, IMIT plans to issue the official response letter to ISA within this week, and we will share it with ISZE once finalized.

 

Thank you for your continued support.

 

Best Regards,

山居

Toshiki Yamai

Subject: RE: [Request for information] Order detail of RG21 & RG30 initial order from ISA to ISZE

 

Dear Peeraya,

 

I have checked and can confirm that the ISA order (361415) was placed on 01/04/26 (for your column G), with the backlog coverage order created immediately as per the standard process. However, ISA did not inform ISZE in advance about the nature of the order and we only became aware after analysing the fill rate. Normally, customers notify ISZE beforehand regarding initial orders and preferably submit a PRD order as it gives us more room for analysis asap. 

 

The order you received in May was intended to build an additional stock buffer from our side following our analysis of their order, rather than to cover any existing backlog. To address the urgency, we also requested to switch some open sea freight orders to air freight, although customer stock order backlog is typically shipped by sea.

 

Finally, could you please advise on IMIT’s communication strategy towards ISA? Will there be an official response from management? We would highly appreciate to keep us in the loop on this so that we can align our message as a group.

 

Kind regards,
Bart

Parts Planning & Inventory Control | ISZE

Hi Masumi,

 

Thank you for your message.

It is indeed likely that this is a breakpoint supersession. However, even in such cases, I assume the catalogue would normally also indicate the latest part number, as illustrated in the example below. The red marking shows the ITC C part, while the yellow marking indicates the latest part number.

As you know, it is IML’s guideline to scrap all ITC C parts accordingly. Given that we still hold stock with a value exceeding EUR 100k, for which our accounting team is now preparing a scrap provision, I believe it can’t hurt to double-check this matter with IMIT to avoid any unnecessary risk.

Better to be safe than sorry in this case (and hopefully keep the stock at year’s end).

 

Kind regards,

Bart

 



 

Bart Van den Bosch

Parts Planning & Inventory Control | ISZE

As we already have the TSI, I doubt if you receive further information.

 

Kind regards,

 

Masumi

Thanks and regards,

 

Masumi

body_preview:
Hello Masumi,

Here is a short summary

Attendees: Yossi Ulmer (VP Aftersales, UTI), Eran Aloni (Parts Manager, UTI), Masumi Hayakawa (Director, ISZE), Jérôme Van der Pluym (Assistant Sales Manager / Pricing Analyst, ISZE)



Backorders — P700: Collision parts and wiring harnesses for the P700 are seeing increasing backorders. Because these parts aren't available, genuine part sales are being undermined — customers turn elsewhere when they can't get the part in time.



P700 Volumes:

*	1,200 P700 trucks sold in 2026
*	~2,000 P700 in total parc by end of 2026





SPA Request: Parallel import and aftersales activity is growing, which strengthens the case for an SPA to keep genuine parts competitive and available.
UTI has sent a counter proposal. ISZE will review it as a total package rather than line by line, with approval to follow hopefully. Final decision sits with the management.



FY2026 Target: New UTI target is around €3.1M for FY2026. UTI is already lagging, driven by parallel import pressure and, in April, the impact of the war with Iran and holidays in Israel.



Visit to ISZE:
UTI will visit ISZE premises in the second week of July. Exact date to be determined.

 

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

subject: ISUZU Code of Conduct
body_preview:
English version (the Dutch translation can be found below)

 

Dear colleagues,

 

Recently, IML introduced a Code of Conduct. This is an important document that provides guidance on how we work, collaborate, and make decisions as an organization.

As this applies to all group companies, we would like to share a summarized version with you.
Thank you in advance for taking this into account. The full PDF version is attached for your reference.

 

At Isuzu, we aim—fully aligned with our vision “Moving the World — for You”—not only to create economic value, but also to make a positive contribution to society and the environment. In a rapidly changing world, where expectations of companies continue to increase, it is essential that we have clear guidelines to help us act responsibly and ethically.

The Code of Conduct provides these guidelines. It is not a strict set of rules, but a practical framework that supports us in our day-to-day work: what we value, how we make decisions, and how we behave in different situations.

 

Who does the Code apply to?

The Code of Conduct applies to all employees and managers within the Isuzu Group. In addition, we expect our suppliers and business partners to understand and respect these principles.

In other words, the Code of Conduct forms a shared foundation for everyone working with and for Isuzu.

 

Our shared responsibility

Trust in Isuzu is not only built on our products or technology, but above all on how we behave every day. Each of us plays an active role in this.

We therefore encourage everyone to:

*	actively use the Code of Conduct as a guideline
*	ask questions when something is unclear
*	report concerns or potential issues in a timely manner

Within Isuzu, several reporting channels are available (e.g. managers, HR, compliance, or external channels). Reports are treated confidentially, and there is explicit protection against negative consequences for anyone who raises concerns in good faith.

 

The role of our leaders

Leaders play a key role in bringing the Code of Conduct to life. They are expected to:

*	lead by example and actively promote our values
*	support employees in making difficult decisions
*	create an open and safe work environment where everyone feels comfortable speaking up
*	report potential violations in a timely and appropriate manner

In addition, they contribute to employee development and foster a culture of dialogue, respect, and collaboration.

 

Key principles in practice

The Code of Conduct is built around several important pillars:

 

1.	Putting customer trust first

We provide high-quality and safe products and services, communicate transparently, and treat customers fairly and with respect. Trust is built through consistent, sincere daily actions.

 

2.	Fair and ethical business conduct

We comply with laws and regulations and act with integrity in all business relationships. This includes:

*	fair competition and transparent cooperation
*	zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, or fraud
*	accurate and transparent communication
*	avoiding relationships with criminal organizations

 

3.	Responsible use of resources and information

We protect company assets and information and use them only for professional purposes. Conflicts of interest are avoided and reported.

 

4.	Respect for one another

We foster a safe, inclusive, and respectful working environment:

*	respect for diversity and equal opportunities
*	no discrimination, harassment, or inappropriate behavior
*	attention to well-being, safety, and a healthy work-life balance

 

5.   Responsibility towards society
We contribute to a sustainable and responsible future by:

*        addressing environmental and climate challenges

*        respecting human rights

*        promoting traffic safety

*        maintaining open dialogue with customers, partners, and society

 

Suppor

body_preview:
Dear Peeraya,

 

Could you please advise on the following matter? I noticed that part number 7552348280 has been assigned ITC (interchangeability) status “C”. This is quite remarkable to say the least, as in February IMIT Service communicated via the attached service bulletin to the distributors to order this part as a countermeasure for the EPS malfunction corrective action.

We currently hold approximately 120 units in stock, representing a value of around €89K. In addition, we already have some stock of the newer part number 7552348300 available (26 pcs).

Hello Masumi,




I would like to escalate the ITUK TCM case, as the current support from IMG Service is not acceptable and is making it impossible to properly support ITUK.

 

Brief timeline / summary

*	ITUK reported a serious TCM issue with a 4 out of 8 failure rate.
*	Several trucks are off-road and ITUK customers are already angry. (now and in the past)
*	The initial concern from ITUK was that they ordered 8984869511, but the units physically showed 8975440040.
*	Ono san confirmed that:

	*	8975440040 is the hardware / production part number;
	*	8984869511 is the service/software part number;
	*	8984869511 is correct for the VIN.

*	Suzuki san also confirmed that:

	*	there is no visible irregularity from a parts sales / shipping point of view;
	*	the service part number is shown on the package label;
	*	similar cases in other markets were caused by incorrect dealer installation, such as bent connector pins or internal circuit damage caused by voltage.

*	Therefore, based on the information received so far, this does not appear to be a simple part number or supply issue.

 

I will just add the e-mail conversation with Rene as attachment, with the last mail as the cherry on the cake where I should contact the supplier of the TCM module.
But I want to show the whole e-mail conversation as I don’t believe this is how IMG & ISZE should cooperate.


At ITUK side this is escalated to Duncan who is on this already for some time and I want to inform you before this get’s escalated further.


We have 4 pieces that arrive here but as 4/8 didn’t work I believe IMG needs to look at this whether it’s an installing issue / part issue or whatever.

I have checked and can confirm that the ISA order (361415) was placed on 01/04/26 (for your column G), with the backlog coverage order created immediately as per the standard process. Hello Nuno,

 

We are locking our units-in-operation figures by market and want to confirm yours directly before we close the numbers.

 

Based on our model, we estimate the following active parc for Portugal as of end-2025:

 

D-max : 5.299

N-Series 2.585
F- Series 292

 

These are derived from cumulative IML/IMIT shipment data convolved against a survival curve — not registration totals. I'd like you to confirm whether these figures look right for your market, or flag where they diverge and why.

 

The scrap rate assumption behind our model:  we apply IMIT's CV survival curve,  see attached.

If your market has a longer or shorter vehicle life — due to used imports, exports, road conditions, or local registration practices — the curve won't apply cleanly and your real active parc will diverge from our estimate. 

If you use a scrap or deregistration rate internally, we kindly ask you to share it with us.

*	Active parc as of 31/12/2025 -> operating vehicles only — not cumulative registrations.

Dear Peeraya,

 

Thank you very much for your information.

Customs may still see the origin of the battery pack as Korean because of following arguments :

*	The essential character of the battery pack comes from the Korean battery cells/modules
*	The IMCT operations are assembly and integration, not manufacturing

 

Therefore, origin remains (out of customs perspective) Korean.
Can you please provide an official Certificate of Origin issued by the Thai Chamber of Commerce (or competent Thai authority) stating TH as the country of origin of the battery pack?
An IMCT/IMIT statement is not enough, as by customs authorities this is seen as an ‘intercompany’ statement , which is rather weak evidence for them to state the origin. 

To support our customs compliance requirements, dear Peeraya san, could you please provide the following:

*	The legal basis or customs rule used to determine Thailand as the non-preferential country of origin
*	An official Certificate of Origin issued by the competent Thai authority indicating Thailand as COO
*	A brief manufacturing process description, including:

	*	components imported from Korea
	*	processing and assembly steps performed in Thailand
	*	estimated value added in Thailand (how much of the final battery pack ‘s value is created by the work and materials added in TH?)

As the goods will be imported into the EU, we need sufficient documentary support in case of customs verification.


What customs want to understand is the following :
What portion of the final sales/manufacturing value of the battery pack comes from TH-origin materials, labour and manufacturing processes?
A simple estimated % breakdown as shown in the example underneath vs. the KR-origin battery modules is sufficient.

If Thai added value is for example 40% (or more) it strengthens the argument that the battery pack is of TH-origin.
If Thai contribution is ‘only’ 10%, it is more likely to say the origin of the battery pack is Korean.

Please provide the CoO by the Thai Chamber of Commerce to prove the Thai Origin, so ISZE can be compliant with customs authorities.

subject: Communicatie HR: Richtlijn loontransparantie
body_preview:
Beste collega’s,

 

De komende periode treedt nieuwe Europese wetgeving rond loontransparantie in werking. 

Deze heeft als doel om meer openheid te creëren rond verloning en het principe van gelijke verloning voor gelijk (waardig) werk verder te versterken.

 

We begrijpen dat dit een belangrijk en soms gevoelig onderwerp is. Transparantie rond verloning raakt aan vertrouwen, duidelijkheid en eerlijkheid – waarden die we binnen ISZE sterk waarderen en verder willen versterken.

 

Wat betekent dit concreet?

*	Werknemers krijgen meer transparantie over hoe lonen worden bepaald
*	Er komt een versterkt recht op informatie over loonstructuren en -criteria
*	Werkgevers moeten kunnen aantonen dat loonverschillen objectief en correct onderbouwd zijn
*	 

Tegelijk willen we ook meegeven dat dit in de praktijk niet altijd eenvoudig is. Binnen onze organisatie zijn er veel verschillende functies en verantwoordelijkheden, waardoor het vergelijken van “gelijk(w)aardig werk” niet altijd evident is. Dit vraagt dus een zorgvuldige en doordachte aanpak.

 

Daarnaast is het belangrijk te benadrukken dat het niet de bedoeling is om individuele lonen van collega’s publiek te maken. 

Om de privacy van iedereen te respecteren (conform GDPR), zullen we werken met groepen of categorieën van functies. We zullen dit op een zo eerlijk en objectief mogelijke manier proberen te realiseren.

 

Op dit moment wachten we nog op de concrete omzetting van deze Europese richtlijn in Belgische wetgeving. Zodra er meer duidelijkheid is over de exacte verplichtingen en timing, zullen wij deze vertalen naar onze eigen processen en communicatie.

Wat mag je van ons verwachten?

*	Heldere en tijdige communicatie over verdere ontwikkelingen
*	Transparantie over de manier waarop ons verloningsbeleid is opgebouwd
*	Een zorgvuldige en respectvolle aanpak, met aandacht voor eerlijkheid én privacy

 

We begrijpen dat dit vragen kan oproepen. Aarzel daarom zeker niet om contact op te nemen met HR – we luisteren graag en gaan graag in dialoog.

 

Korte Q&A

1. Zal ik het loon van mijn collega’s kunnen zien?
Nee. Het is niet de bedoeling dat individuele lonen openbaar worden gemaakt. We zullen werken met gegroepeerde data (bv. per functieniveau of categorie), zodat de privacy van iedereen beschermd blijft.

2. Wat betekent “gelijkwaardig werk”?
Gelijkwaardig werk verwijst naar functies die vergelijkbaar zijn qua verantwoordelijkheden, vereiste vaardigheden, ervaring en impact. Omdat onze organisatie veel verschillende jobs telt, is dit niet altijd eenvoudig en vraagt dit een zorgvuldige beoordeling.

3. Kan ik informatie opvragen over verloning?
De wetgeving voorziet dat werknemers bepaalde informatie kunnen opvragen. Hoe dit concreet zal verlopen binnen onze organisatie, zal verder verduidelijkt worden zodra de Belgische wetgeving definitief is.

4. Wat gebeurt er als er loonverschillen zijn?
Loonverschillen zijn mogelijk, maar moeten steeds objectief en correct onderbouwd zijn (bv. ervaring, rol, performance, marktevolutie…). Dit blijven we ook in de toekomst zorgvuldig bewaken.

 

Indien er vragen zijn, aarzel niet om me te contacteren.

Met vriendelijke groeten,

subject: RE: [urgent request] Battery Module P/N 7552125550
body_preview:
Dear Peeraya,

 

Thank you very much for your information.

Customs may still see the origin of the battery pack as Korean because of following arguments :

*	The essential character of the battery pack comes from the Korean battery cells/modules
*	The IMCT operations are assembly and integration, not manufacturing

 

Therefore, origin remains (out of customs perspective) Korean.
Can you please provide an official Certificate of Origin issued by the Thai Chamber of Commerce (or competent Thai authority) stating TH as the country of origin of the battery pack?
An IMCT/IMIT statement is not enough, as by customs authorities this is seen as an ‘intercompany’ statement , which is rather weak evidence for them to state the origin. 

To support our customs compliance requirements, dear Peeraya san, could you please provide the following:

*	The legal basis or customs rule used to determine Thailand as the non-preferential country of origin
*	An official Certificate of Origin issued by the competent Thai authority indicating Thailand as COO
*	A brief manufacturing process description, including:

	*	components imported from Korea
	*	processing and assembly steps performed in Thailand
	*	estimated value added in Thailand (how much of the final battery pack ‘s value is created by the work and materials added in TH?)

As the goods will be imported into the EU, we need sufficient documentary support in case of customs verification.


What customs want to understand is the following :
What portion of the final sales/manufacturing value of the battery pack comes from TH-origin materials, labour and manufacturing processes?
A simple estimated % breakdown as shown in the example underneath vs. the KR-origin battery modules is sufficient.

Dear Peeraya san

 

Thank you very much for your explanation.

The assembly process is not always enough to ‘change’ the origin from KR to TH.

The question that should be asked is :
Does the assembly in Thailand amount to a “substantial transformation” of the Korean-made battery modules/cells?
If IMCT mainly:

*	installs Korean battery modules into a housing, 
*	adds wiring, connectors, BMS, cooling components, 
*	performs testing and packaging, 

then this is often considered as assembly, not a substantial transformation.

Customs rulings on battery packs conclude that the battery modules provide the essential character and assembling modules into one pack does NOT change origin.

Could you please investigate the above internally?
