Dear all,

 

This is an update regarding the ISZE portal attack and the recovery plan.

As already informed and discussed with our Sales colleagues, we had a follow-up meeting yesterday with IML, ISZE IT, and the Directors.

As communicated earlier, the plan was to start using the current QA server as a temporary workaround from yesterday onward. However, this plan was ultimately rejected by the IML Risk Management Department.

The main reason is that, since the attack appears to have started in August last year, there is a possibility that the QA server may also have been affected. As this server is located in the Fujisawa Data Center, where core systems for the entire Isuzu Group worldwide are running, we do not want to take the risk of using it, even as a temporary solution.

The current status and plan are as follows:

 

The compromised server will be decommissioned and rebuilt from scratch.

The reconstruction will proceed in two phases:

 

1.	Phase 1 – Interim recovery measure
	To enable early recovery, a new server with the same configuration will be built and brought into operation at the Inzai Data Center, replacing the current Fujisawa Data Center setup.
2.	Phase 2 – Long-term solution
	As a permanent solution, the security architecture will be redesigned to address increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, and the system will be rebuilt on AWS to ensure a higher level of security.

 

The estimated timeline is approximately 10 days for Phase 1 and about 3 months for Phase 2, starting from the design phase.

We regret to inform you that the server outage is expected to continue for approximately two weeks, and we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this may cause. During this period, we kindly ask for your cooperation with the following temporary measures:

 

1.	Order placement
	Please continue sending the two Excel files (Header + Item) to systemplanning@isuzu-e.com <mailto:systemplanning@isuzu-e.com>  if you would like us to upload the orders. Please always double-check the data before sending it to IT.
2.	Stock data
	Stock files will be sent to customers by email as a temporary solution.
3.	Order status updates
	We will develop a program to extract order status for each customer from the SAP Sales Cockpit report and automatically send it by email to the recipients maintained in the customer BP in SAP with the ACK (Order Acknowledgements) parameter. This should be ready within a few days.
4.	GDPR reporting
	The reporting process to the authorities consists of two steps. The first step, which had to be completed within 72 hours, was already completed on 7 April. From that date, we have 21 days to complete the second and final step, which is more detailed and must be submitted on behalf of ISZE as a company.

At the moment, I am encountering some difficulties completing this second step, as I do not have the necessary authorization to log in to the authority portal on behalf of ISZE. Most likely, the login will need to be performed by Masumi, who is officially registered with the authorities for ISZE. I will check this with Masumi on Friday.

 

This is the latest status. I will, of course, keep everyone informed of any further updates.

 

Best regards,
ISZE IT & IML ERP Solution Expert Department

body_preview:
Dear colleagues,

 

During past weeks, you might have heard news surrounding our IML/ISZE Web Portal potential breach or the Basic-Fit gym that has been breached and millions of personal data was leaked, we will start to gradually implement more security measures.

One of those measures for now is MFA for our Microsoft environment, this has already been done with a small control group (Department Managers) for follow-up purposes, and we have now reached the phase of enrolling it companywide.
This will start in the upcoming days.

What this means for you:
Once a day, you will be asked to use your phone (Microsoft authenticator app) to confirm the sign-in when trying to access Microsoft Teams/Outlook on your laptop:




Nasir and I will be assisting you closely so you will not have to configure the MFA yourself in case that you do not have it; the implementation itself should not take longer than 10 minutes if needed.

In case you would have any questions surrounding the implementation or you would encounter any issues, please feel free to let us know.


Thank you for your understanding.



 

Met vriendelijke groeten,
With kind regards,
Bien cordialement,

 

Patrick Csikos

Hi, Jérôme,

 

Thanks for the heads-up.

Shall we have a chat tomorrow (14 Apr)?

I think I am free all day.

 

My first thought is that it is not a good idea to mix the two issues.

I also think IML has the responsibility to explain first why the wrong price was registered.

 

I understand you guys have been on this case for some time, but can you straighten up from the scratch for me?

 

NOx sensor overstock:

Incorrect PN supersession information is the cause.

IML should therefore in theory compensate the loss (overstock).

Overstock at ISZE = xxx pcs (xxx EUR)., ITUK = xxx pcs (xxx EUR)

CR should be issued by IML to ISZE for the total overstock quantity and amount. 

CR should then be issued by ISZE to ITUK for ITUK’s overstock.

 

However, IML does not want to issue CR, as they have no budget for this kind of expenditure. 

 

As a workaround, ISZE can provide SPA on some items to ITUK. The total amount from the SPA equals the overstock of NOx sensors.

 

Error in DPD purchase price

IML has made an error on the DPD price, and invoices ISZE with the wrong price for which ISZE has already paid.

IML wants to recuperate the loss.

ISZE can refuse their request.

 

However, the accumulated amount from the price error is too large to ignore (xxx pcs, xxx EUR). 

 

How can you connect the SPA amount we provide to ITUK, and compensation from IML which is cancelled out by IML’s price error?

Additionally, we need to be able to explain ISZE’s accounting.

 

I think IML needs to come up with a package to explain.

 

Masumi

Subject: RE: Business impact of the Iran conflict

 

Dear Ling. 

 

These questions are a bit hard to answer as the full impact that this case might have on the country has not fully come to effect. 

 

However, what we are seeing is that for example prices on gasoline and diesel have increased by 13%, which leads to higher prices on food and transportation of all sorts of goods.

This increase also leads to an increase of inflation, meaning that loans for new vehicles and housing are higher. 

 

Luckily for us the motor oil we use is manufactured in Europe, so we are currently not forecasting any shortage there. 

 

Regards to Isuzu we are not forecasting any big changes as many of NCS are sold to businesses and government, and also in terms of collision which is paid for by insurance companies should not be affected much. 

What we might see regarding the supply change is higher transport cost on goods to Iceland so we might be facing higher parts pricing making us less competitive to the AM. 

On top of that if Isuzu starts to increase the price from there end as well we will be out of the game. 

 

Our biggest concern regarding Isuzu at the moment is the cyber-attack on your IT systems, making us less operational when it comes to stock status, ordering and pricing.   

 

Gasoline price development, approximately 1,5€ pr L today, note that additional to the price on the pump every vehicle needs to pay 0,05€ for each driven km, meaning 5€ pr 100 km. 

That can mean extra 50€ approximately a month in taxation for a normal household. 

 

Again, this is all a forecast and what we can predict at the moment, things can change very quickly.

 



 

 

Bestu kveðjur / Best regards,

Hi Koen,

 

Please be advised that Stephen McCaffrey and Neil Mahon no longer work for the Harris Group. 

 

I would be open to an introductory discussion on this. As you know we currently source our oils and lubricants from local suppliers which has served us well to date, we recognise there are potential advantages to aligning more closely with Isuzu's own branded products and would be interested in exploring what that could look like. A manufacturer-backed lubricant would provide greater assurance of compatibility and performance across the Isuzu range. If the pricing is competitive there is potential. 

 

That said, we would want to be transparent about a number of considerations important to us. Our current local suppliers offer favourable terms, so any Isuzu-supplied solution would need to be genuinely competitive. Not just on price, but factoring in delivery costs, lead times, and minimum order quantities to Ireland. We would also need to manage any transition carefully to avoid disruption to our operations,

Dear Suzuki san,

Thank you for your time this week it was a pleasure to meet with you and thank you for the wrap up document.

I would like to point out one item regarding the maintenance interval, the information you have detailed shows NLR85, this is for the previous N35.120 model with the 4JJ1 engine which we haven’t sold for quite a number of years.

To be successful, I think we should focus on the newer models which are the N35.125 and N35.150 which have the RZ4E and 4JZ1 engines respectively.

Based on this, please refer to the owner’s manual that reflects the NLR87 which is the RZ4E engine and has a maintenance interval of 20,000kms and the NLR88 which has a flexible maintenance interval up to 40,000kms.

Also, these are all 3.5t vehicles which we know are difficult to locate and my understanding was that we would look at targeting 7.5t customers primarily fleet customers where we see the greatest potential opportunity whereby both engine types 4JZ1 and 4HK1 NPR88 and NPR75 respectively both have a maintenance interval of 40,000kms.

If you need some further support with the maintenance intervals and model types, please let me know.

I will also as agreed look at our average brake pad replacement cycle based on 7.5t for vehicles on R&M and let you know.

Kind Regards

Tim

body_preview:
Dear Ling,



thank you for reaching out and for the opportunity to share our assessment regarding the potential business impact arising from the ongoing conflict involving Iran. Based on our current observations, we would like to summarize our views as follows:

Financial Impact
We anticipate increased transportation and logistics costs, primarily driven by rising fuel prices and higher risk premiums in international transport. Depending on further developments, we estimate an increase in transport-related costs in the high single‑digit to low double‑digit percentage range. At the same time, weakened demand on the vehicle market may exert pressure on revenues.

Qualitative Impact
Beyond the direct financial effects, we observe a growing level of uncertainty among customers. The geopolitical situation is contributing to a generally more cautious purchasing behavior, particularly for higher-value investments such as vehicles. This is likely to result in delayed purchase decisions and longer sales cycles.

Macroeconomic Impact
The conflict is expected to further dampen overall economic sentiment. Higher energy and fuel costs reduce consumers’ disposable income and may contribute to slowing economic growth. This environment increases the likelihood of a broader cooling of demand across the automotive sector.

Supply Chain and Logistics Impact
From a logistics perspective, we expect higher transportation costs and potentially longer lead times due to increased fuel prices and possible disruptions or rerouting in international transport corridors. While no immediate supply shortages are evident at this stage, indirect impacts on availability and costs cannot be ruled out if the situation escalates.

 

Mit freundlichen Grüßen / Best regards

Good Morning Ling,

 

Apologies for not coming back sooner.

 

Having spoken to John, we are not aware of any major disturbances to our business caused by the conflict in the middle East. 

 

The UK has seen large rises in fuel prices in recent weeks, this will of course affect the motor trade but as for a direct impact on our business this is a fairly small amount at present. If prices continue to rise at the current rate then this could develop into a larger issue. However, the burden is more on the end user of the vehicle in regard to fuel prices, this really only affects IUK in relation to internal vehicles such as events and press fleet. 

 

As for shipping delays and increased costs, we have not seen any great impact here either. The majority of our containers are shipped around the cape of South Africa so the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has not had much of an impact on us.

 

Of course this is something the business will be keeping a close eye on and should there be any significant updates we will be sure to let you know.

subject: RE: Business impact of the Iran conflict
body_preview:
Dear Ling,

 

Financial Impact

At this stage, we anticipate a moderate negative financial impact, primarily driven by increased logistics and transportation costs. Disruptions to key global shipping routes may result in freight cost increases in the region of 15 - 30%, depending on duration and severity. In addition, extended lead times may increase working capital requirements due to higher pipeline inventory.

We also note potential margin pressure, as the ability to fully pass on cost increases to the Irish market may be limited in the short term.

 

Qualitative Impact

From an operational and commercial perspective, the main impact is expected to be increased uncertainty in supply chain reliability rather than absolute shortages. 

 

This may lead to:

Reduced visibility on delivery timelines and planning

Increased complexity in managing dealer expectations and stock levels

Potential delays in customer purchasing decisions due to market uncertainty

Additional pressure on maintaining consistent vehicle availability across the network

 

We do not currently foresee any structural or strategic disruption to the business, but the situation may impact short-term operational efficiency.

 

Macroeconomic Impact

The Irish economy remains relatively resilient; however, we anticipate indirect effects arising from increased energy prices and inflationary pressures.

Higher fuel costs and persistent inflation may affect consumer and SME confidence, which could result in moderate softening of demand, particularly in sectors such as construction and small business fleets. At this stage, we expect this to be a slowdown in growth rather than a contraction.

 

Supply Chain and Logistics Impact

We expect the most significant impact to arise indirectly through global shipping disruptions. 

 

Any instability affecting key maritime routes may lead to:

Extended transit times from production origins into Europe

Increased variability in shipment schedules and arrival patterns

Knock-on delays within European processing hubs, including Belgium

Less predictable supply flow into Ireland, with potential for uneven vehicle availability

 

At present, we do not anticipate a complete interruption to supply, but rather reduced consistency and longer lead times.

 

Summary

Overall, the expected impact is moderate and primarily indirect, characterised by increased costs, longer and less predictable lead times, and some softening in market demand.

 

 

Regards,

body_preview:
Dear Ling. 

 

These questions are a bit hard to answer as the full impact that this case might have on the country has not fully come to effect. 

 

However, what we are seeing is that for example prices on gasoline and diesel have increased by 13%, which leads to higher prices on food and transportation of all sorts of goods.

This increase also leads to an increase of inflation, meaning that loans for new vehicles and housing are higher. 

 

Luckily for us the motor oil we use is manufactured in Europe, so we are currently not forecasting any shortage there. 

 

Regards to Isuzu we are not forecasting any big changes as many of NCS are sold to businesses and government, and also in terms of collision which is paid for by insurance companies should not be affected much. 

What we might see regarding the supply change is higher transport cost on goods to Iceland so we might be facing higher parts pricing making us less competitive to the AM. 

On top of that if Isuzu starts to increase the price from there end as well we will be out of the game. 

 

Our biggest concern regarding Isuzu at the moment is the cyber-attack on your IT systems, making us less operational when it comes to stock status, ordering and pricing.   

 

Gasoline price development, approximately 1,5€ pr L today, note that additional to the price on the pump every vehicle needs to pay 0,05€ for each driven km, meaning 5€ pr 100 km. 

That can mean extra 50€ approximately a month in taxation for a normal household. 

 

Again, this is all a forecast and what we can predict at the moment, things can change very quickly.

Regarding the ongoing conflict involving Iran and the USA–Israel, we would like to inform you that there has been no significant impact on our aftersales operations. The overall volume of work in this segment remains stable and in line with previous periods.

Dear Valued Customer,

 

We have been requested to conduct an assessment of the potential business impact arising from the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

In this context, we kindly invite you to share your views and insights on the following aspects:

 

*	Financial Impact: Estimated financial effects, where possible expressed as absolute values and/or percentages.
*	Qualitative Impact: Relevant non-financial implications, including operational, commercial, or strategic considerations.
*	Macroeconomic Impact: Observed or anticipated effects on national economic indicators, such as GDP or similar economic indicators.
*	Supply Chain and Logistics Impact (physical impact/conditional impact): Any current or expected impact on supply availability, transportation, lead times, or other logistical conditions, whether direct or indirect.

 

Please be assured that all information shared will be treated as strictly confidential and used solely for internal reporting purposes to our management.

 

We would appreciate it if you could share the requested information by Friday, 10th April 2026.

 

Thank you in advance for your cooperation and support.

subject: Update on Web Portal Recovery, Permanent Solution, and GDPR Status
body_preview:
Dear all,

 

I would like to provide you with an update following meetings this morning with the Japan Infrastructure team and management, as well as with the IML GDPR Department and DPO.

 

1.	Server recovery status
	We have agreed with IML to temporarily use the QA web server, which was not connected to the network, in order to restore operations and allow customers to access the portal again.
	The data (accounts and related data) will be copied from the production server to the QA server on Friday and during the weekend. Our target is to have the portal available again from Monday the 13th.

It has not yet been fully confirmed, but the portal URL will most likely remain the same. However, it may be necessary for users to reset their passwords on Monday. I will confirm and update you accordingly.

Until then, please continue to ask customers to submit their orders via Excel files, as previously communicated.

2.	Permanent solution
	While restoring access via the QA server as a temporary measure, we are also working in parallel on defining a permanent solution. Several options are currently being evaluated.
	The main priority at this stage remains restoring access for customers as quickly as possible.
3.	GDPR
	I had a meeting with the IML GDPR Department and reviewed the actions taken. Yesterday afternoon, ISZE submitted the official notification (Step 1) to the Belgian authorities.

The next step (Step 2) must be completed within 21 days. I plan to complete this final step next week.

As confirmed by the IML GDPR Department, the actions taken so far are compliant with GDPR requirements. Since the potentially affected data is limited to company names and email addresses, the incident is classified as low risk.

 

I will provide further updates as soon as there is more clarity regarding point 1.

 

Kind regards,
Jimmy

IML has confirmed that the current production web portal server cannot be reopened at this stage. Recent findings from the M23 Infrastructure Team indicate signs of unauthorized access dating back to last year.

The server is hosted in the Fujisawa Data Center, where IML’s core business systems are also located. Reconnecting the external network at this point would pose a high risk to other systems in the same environment.

According to the investigation, the incident was most likely caused by unauthorized access exploiting an application vulnerability.

body_preview:
Dear Suzuki san,

 

I understand IML’s concern. However, for Bosch parts, the logistics process is different.

 

Parts produced in the US, such as PM sensors, are first transported to the Bosch warehouse in Germany.

From there, they are shipped to Bosch Japan, then to IML, and finally to ISZE. These parts are not shipped directly from the US to Japan, except when they are intended for production use.

 

As mentioned in my previous email, Bosch manages production (OEM) parts and aftersales (service) parts as two separate business lines. As a result, these parts follow different supply routes.

 

Because the parts are already shipped to Bosch Germany first, it would mean that if we continue buying them from IML, the parts will travel from the EU (Bosch Germany) to JP (Bosch JP) and from JP (IML) back to the EU (ISZE).

 

This is an additional unnecessary travel time of 4,5 months (Sea freight from DE --> JP = 2 months; from Bosch JP --> IML = 1-2 weeks; from JP --> BE = 2 months). This travel lead time does not include any additional warehouse processing at Bosch JP, at IML and at ISZE.

On top of that, it would mean double transport costs and double import duties (once for Bosch JP and again for ISZE). 

If we add the additional profit margins (Bosch JP, IML and ISZE), these parts will become too expensive and no longer competitive in the market.

It is also not the most environmentally friendly way to supply a part if we ship it around the world before we sell it to our customers.

 

By contrast, these parts can be sourced directly from another Bosch dealer in the EU at a significantly lower cost (no import duties, no transport costs to JP and back and minimum profit Margins) and with no 4-5 months of additional lead time.

 

The above arguments were the main reasons for starting the direct supply of the two PM sensors for the Service replacement.

If we continued to only purchase these sensors from IML, our customers would have to wait about 8-9 months in total for a Service repair and warranty part, which would have been catastrophic for our company’s reputation. This could have caused customers to choose another brand in the future.

 

We also need to keep in mind that with the current political climate, the transport costs and lead times will increase significantly.

I hope you can understand why these parts with US source as Bosch aftersales parts are included in this list.

 

For the complete list (incl non-Bosch parts) and the other points raised in your previous email, I need to check a few things internally first.

 

Thank you, 

 

 

Best Regards,

Subject: IMPORTANT: Update on IML/ISZE Web Portal Outage and Temporary Measures
Importance: High

 

Dear all,

 

This is an important update regarding the ISZE web portal outage following the cyber attack on the IML side.

IML has confirmed that the current production web portal server cannot be reopened at this stage. Recent findings from the M23 Infrastructure Team indicate signs of unauthorized access dating back to last year.

The server is hosted in the Fujisawa Data Center, where IML’s core business systems are also located. Reconnecting the external network at this point would pose a high risk to other systems in the same environment.

According to the investigation, the incident was most likely caused by unauthorized access exploiting an application vulnerability.

As a temporary measure, IML is rebuilding the server using the latest OS version and will only make it available again once all security patches have been applied and vulnerabilities have been eliminated. subject: IMPORTANT: Update on IML/ISZE Web Portal Outage and Temporary Measures
body_preview:
Dear all,

 

This is an important update regarding the ISZE web portal outage following the cyber attack on the IML side.

IML has confirmed that the current production web portal server cannot be reopened at this stage. Recent findings from the M23 Infrastructure Team indicate signs of unauthorized access dating back to last year.

The server is hosted in the Fujisawa Data Center, where IML’s core business systems are also located. Reconnecting the external network at this point would pose a high risk to other systems in the same environment.

According to the investigation, the incident was most likely caused by unauthorized access exploiting an application vulnerability.

As a temporary measure, IML is rebuilding the server using the latest OS version and will only make it available again once all security patches have been applied and vulnerabilities have been eliminated. Although the rebuild has already started, IML cannot yet guarantee a smooth recovery. At this stage, the estimated timeline is at least two weeks, although all efforts will be made to shorten this period.

For the long-term solution, IML is considering rebuilding the web portal in the AWS Tokyo Region with a more secure architecture, including enhanced security controls to prevent direct external exposure of IP addresses.

This incident has also been escalated within IML to Ohtani-san (NQ5) and Director Shide-san (NQ0).

 

________________________________

Temporary Business Continuity Measures (ISZE)

As the web portal is currently unavailable and some ISZE customers rely on it, we have implemented a temporary solution for sales order creation in SAP:

*	The majority of Vehicle Parts (VP) customers use EDI, which remains fully operational and unaffected. These customers will not experience any impact.
*	Customers who normally use the web portal are requested to submit orders via Excel files (Header and Item level).

Please find attached the required file formats and examples.

Customers can send the Excel files to the ISZE Sales team by email. For today, the Sales team is requested to forward these emails to:
systemplanning@isuzu-e.com <mailto:systemplanning@isuzu-e.com> 

Jimmy and Nasir will handle the uploads initially. Later today, access will be configured so that the Sales team can perform the uploads directly in SAP.

Until then, the IT team will continue to support by processing all uploads.

We kindly ask the Sales team to inform customers who normally use the portal to send both Excel files (Header and Item) for order placement until the portal has been fully restored.

 

Further updates will follow as more information becomes available.

 

Best regards,
Jimmy

Dear Niklas

 

As manufacturer, Isuzu is currently evaluating the integration of the lubricant business into our overall European business structure.

 

The objective of this initiative is twofold. On the one hand, we aim to further optimize the quality of the lubricants used across our network. 

On the other hand, we see clear potential to increase turnover and profit margins for all parties involved, while at the same time reducing overall costs.

This will be accompanied by the creation of a new Isuzu-branded oil.

 

This approach has already been successfully implemented in other regions, where it has delivered tangible benefits both commercially and operationally. 

Based on these positive experiences, we would now like to involve our European distributors in exploring similar opportunities.

 

Our guiding principle in this project is clear: the goal must always be to maintain at least the same or comparable 

advantages as today — or to achieve improved benefits. And this always at a more competitive price level.

 

At this stage, we are approaching the largest European markets to assess initial interest. 

Please note that we are not asking for any commitment at this moment. 

The purpose of this communication is solely to explore whether there is interest in an introductory discussion to map the current situation,

including existing agreements, benefits, and specific needs.

 

Based on these discussions, we can then evaluate whether there is a willingness to participate in the next step of the process, 

potentially leading to involvement in a price tender in a later stage.

 

We would highly appreciate your feedback by on whether you would be open to a first exchange on this topic.

Please be advised that Stephen McCaffrey and Neil Mahon no longer work for the Harris Group. 

 

I would be open to an introductory discussion on this. As you know we currently source our oils and lubricants from local suppliers which has served us well to date, we recognise there are potential advantages to aligning more closely with Isuzu's own branded products and would be interested in exploring what that could look like. A manufacturer-backed lubricant would provide greater assurance of compatibility and performance across the Isuzu range. If the pricing is competitive there is potential.

Dear Suzuki san,

 

Please allow me to step in and address your question.

*	Deviation in sales amount (February – IE parts):
	The sales figures we share with you each month are based on the sales dataset extracted directly from our system. These figures can sometimes differ from the final accounting results, which are only available approximately one week later. The final accounting figures include provisions and other adjustments that may impact the outcome. Once available, the final figures are updated in our Power BI records, which is why any differences may become visible in the following month. In the case of February, we are currently reviewing the discrepancy with the accounting team, as we believe there may be an error in their analysis. They are investigating and will revert shortly. If incorrect, we will update the result shortly in PBI.
*	Small differences in order amounts:
	Our datasets are extracted from the system on a monthly basis and remain unchanged thereafter. At the end of the financial year, we typically perform a full refresh of the data for the entire FY to capture minor changes (such as cancellations) that occurred after the initial extraction, ensuring the most accurate data possible.

Bart

Dear Suzuki san,

 

Please allow me to step in and address your question.

*	Deviation in sales amount (February – IE parts):
	The sales figures we share with you each month are based on the sales dataset extracted directly from our system. These figures can sometimes differ from the final accounting results, which are only available approximately one week later. The final accounting figures include provisions and other adjustments that may impact the outcome. Once available, the final figures are updated in our Power BI records, which is why any differences may become visible in the following month. In the case of February, we are currently reviewing the discrepancy with the accounting team, as we believe there may be an error in their analysis. They are investigating and will revert shortly. If incorrect, we will update the result shortly in PBI.
*	Small differences in order amounts:
	Our datasets are extracted from the system on a monthly basis and remain unchanged thereafter. At the end of the financial year, we typically perform a full refresh of the data for the entire FY to capture minor changes (such as cancellations) that occurred after the initial extraction, ensuring the most accurate data possible.

body_preview:
Dear Suzuki san,

 

Please allow me to step in and address your question.

*	Deviation in sales amount (February – IE parts):
	The sales figures we share with you each month are based on the sales dataset extracted directly from our system. These figures can sometimes differ from the final accounting results, which are only available approximately one week later. The final accounting figures include provisions and other adjustments that may impact the outcome. Once available, the final figures are updated in our Power BI records, which is why any differences may become visible in the following month. In the case of February, we are currently reviewing the discrepancy with the accounting team, as we believe there may be an error in their analysis. They are investigating and will revert shortly. If incorrect, we will update the result shortly in PBI.
*	Small differences in order amounts:
	Our datasets are extracted from the system on a monthly basis and remain unchanged thereafter. At the end of the financial year, we typically perform a full refresh of the data for the entire FY to capture minor changes (such as cancellations) that occurred after the initial extraction, ensuring the most accurate data possible.

 

Kind regards,
Bart

Parts Planning & Inventory Control | ISZE

Dear Hadi,

 

As mentioned before, I would like you to create urgently the action plans for the coming term.

The key points are:

*	Genuine parts share expansion

	*	Incentive programme to roll out
	*	Incorporating into the distributor’s parts business plan
	*	PMS parts promotion

*	R&M promotion

	*	Incentive programme to roll out
	*	Raising awareness, market intelligence, identifying gaps, sharing findings with IMG

*	IDS activities

	*	Planning of the dealer improvement activities

*	Parts training

	*	Schedule confirmation

		*	Training structure (table of course contents)
		*	Contents development
		*	Trial 
		*	Rollout

	*	Create road map for parts competition

		*	Survey
		*	Design, steps/phases

*	Lubricant business

	*	Action plan documentation

		*	Who does what, when and how

 

The most urgent is ISZE’s action plan on PMS parts promotion, as we are planning to visit ITUK (TVS).

We need to determine how ISZE incorporates PMS project into our business plan, before we meet with Suzuki san and Duncan next week.

 

Let’s discuss this at the earliest convenience – I am more or less free today and tomorrow. Can you send me a Teams invite for a time slot you and Jérôme are free?

 

Additionally, although it is not in the key action plans, we need to identify the parts sales potential on IE parts in order to fine tune our business planning. 

For this exercise, the following information are necessary:

*	Machine population
*	Replacement interval

Let’s also discuss this separately, with Peter and Ling. Please can you send out an invite?

 

Thanks,

 

Masumi

Subject: Pricing errors + cab situation

 

Dear all,

I wanted to follow up on two issues that are currently impacting our day-to-day operations and, more broadly, our ability to grow parts sales in line with Isuzu's 2030 targets. (cabs)

 

Pricing error resolution — TH-sourced parts

Since the Salesforce integration, we've lost the ability to look up TH-sourced parts on the IML website. This has created a gap we can't work around: the IML site displays the price class for a part, which is essential for resolving pricing errors. That information doesn't appear on the IMIT website, so for TH-sourced parts, we currently have no way to correct pricing errors. Could you advise on how you'd like us to handle this in the interim, and whether there's a timeline for restoring this visibility? I believe informing ASC before new functionalities of (the lack of functionalities) could have prevented this situation.

 

 

Cab ordering process

We raised a ticket on this 801 days ago. I appreciate that this project takes time, and that this was but we've had very little visibility into where things stand — follow-up requests for updates have gone unanswered. Given that a more efficient cab ordering process would have a direct positive impact on sales volumes, this feels like an area where progress would benefit both sides. Any update on status or expected timeline would be genuinely helpful.

 

 

We would appreciate a response on both points so we can find a path forward.

 

Kind regards,

subject: Pricing errors + cab situation
body_preview:
Dear all,

I wanted to follow up on two issues that are currently impacting our day-to-day operations and, more broadly, our ability to grow parts sales in line with Isuzu's 2030 targets. (cabs)

 

Pricing error resolution — TH-sourced parts

Since the Salesforce integration, we've lost the ability to look up TH-sourced parts on the IML website. This has created a gap we can't work around: the IML site displays the price class for a part, which is essential for resolving pricing errors. That information doesn't appear on the IMIT website, so for TH-sourced parts, we currently have no way to correct pricing errors. Could you advise on how you'd like us to handle this in the interim, and whether there's a timeline for restoring this visibility? I believe informing ASC before new functionalities of (the lack of functionalities) could have prevented this situation.

 

 

Cab ordering process

We raised a ticket on this 801 days ago. I appreciate that this project takes time, and that this was but we've had very little visibility into where things stand — follow-up requests for updates have gone unanswered. Given that a more efficient cab ordering process would have a direct positive impact on sales volumes, this feels like an area where progress would benefit both sides. Any update on status or expected timeline would be genuinely helpful.

 

 

We would appreciate a response on both points so we can find a path forward.

 

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Dear Hadi,

 

As mentioned before, I would like you to create urgently the action plans for the coming term.

The key points are:

*	Genuine parts share expansion

	*	Incentive programme to roll out
	*	Incorporating into the distributor’s parts business plan
	*	PMS parts promotion

*	R&M promotion

	*	Incentive programme to roll out
	*	Raising awareness, market intelligence, identifying gaps, sharing findings with IMG

*	IDS activities

	*	Planning of the dealer improvement activities

*	Parts training

	*	Schedule confirmation

		*	Training structure (table of course contents)
		*	Contents development
		*	Trial 
		*	Rollout

	*	Create road map for parts competition

		*	Survey
		*	Design, steps/phases

*	Lubricant business

	*	Action plan documentation

		*	Who does what, when and how

 

The most urgent is ISZE’s action plan on PMS parts promotion, as we are planning to visit ITUK (TVS).

We need to determine how ISZE incorporates PMS project into our business plan, before we meet with Suzuki san and Duncan next week.

 

Let’s discuss this at the earliest convenience – I am more or less free today and tomorrow. Can you send me a Teams invite for a time slot you and Jérôme are free?

 

Additionally, although it is not in the key action plans, we need to identify the parts sales potential on IE parts in order to fine tune our business planning. 

For this exercise, the following information are necessary:

*	Machine population
*	Replacement interval

Let’s also discuss this separately, with Peter and Ling. Please can you send out an invite?

 

Thanks,

 

Masumi

Dear all,

 

ISZE will start running a parts training session and want your team there.

 

The focus is EQ-Hit — how to use it properly, how it directly affects the ordering accuracy, using genuine parts numbers and BVP parts. We'll keep it practical and make sure there's time to work through your specific situation.

 

One thing worth flagging: dealer staff turnover is a recurring cost for your dealership’s organisation. Every time a parts person moves on, your team ends up back at the dealer covering the same ground. The intent of this training is to give dealers a stronger operational foundation — reducing that dependency and the resource overhead that comes with it each time.

 

This isn't a box-ticking exercise. Parts profitability is a real growth lever for your dealers, and lowering your own support burden in the process is worth taking seriously.

body_preview:
Hi Koen,

 

Please be advised that Stephen McCaffrey and Neil Mahon no longer work for the Harris Group. 

 

I would be open to an introductory discussion on this. As you know we currently source our oils and lubricants from local suppliers which has served us well to date, we recognise there are potential advantages to aligning more closely with Isuzu's own branded products and would be interested in exploring what that could look like. A manufacturer-backed lubricant would provide greater assurance of compatibility and performance across the Isuzu range. If the pricing is competitive there is potential. 

 

That said, we would want to be transparent about a number of considerations important to us. Our current local suppliers offer favourable terms, so any Isuzu-supplied solution would need to be genuinely competitive. Not just on price, but factoring in delivery costs, lead times, and minimum order quantities to Ireland. We would also need to manage any transition carefully to avoid disruption to our operations, and we would want clarity on whether any exclusivity is expected.

Dear Shahaf,

 

We wanted to inform you that invoice 202647704 has been selected by customs for physical inspection prior to release.

 

Given the circumstances, we have taken the decision to exclude this invoice from the current shipment. Our reasoning is as follows:

 

Arranging shipments to your market is logistically complex given the current situation and the current consignment is relatively small at +-3 loading meters.
Our warehouse is also at overcapacity at this time, meaning we cannot hold back the remainder of the shipment while the inspected invoice awaits customs clearance — the timeline for that process is unpredictable.

 

We also considered that a partial delivery on this invoice would likely not serve you well, as the remaining parts on the shipment would be needed and this also has an impact on UMI parts.

 

The other invoices in this shipment will proceed as planned. Invoice 202647704 will be included in the next available shipment once customs has cleared it.

Dear Suzuki-san,

 

Thank you very much for your message and for the detailed investigation.

 

It is correct that we currently maintain a healthy margin.
However, a price adjustment is strategically important for us at this stage, and I would like to outline the key business reasons behind this request.

 

1. Safeguarding sales volume for ageing Stage 3A machines
Most short block sales today are for Stage 3A models, which are approaching the later stages of their economic lifecycle. 

Owners of these machines are extremely cost‑sensitive. If the repair cost is too high, they often choose to scrap the machine rather than invest in an engine replacement.
In these cases, we lose not only the short block sale, but also future parts turnover for that machine.
Competitive pricing helps keep these units operational, which ultimately supports Isuzu’s long‑term installed base in Europe.

 

2. Preventing market loss to low‑cost alternatives
End users increasingly compare our prices with local remanufactured engines and complete overhauls built with cheap copy parts.
If our price gap becomes too wide, customers choose these alternatives, and we lose the entire opportunity.
By keeping short block pricing attractive, we retain the business within the Isuzu ecosystem, ensuring reliability, quality perception, and customer loyalty.

 

3. Strategic importance of the new Industrial Long Block project
We are preparing to launch a new Industrial Long Block concept.
Due to the many variations in flywheel housings, a fully assembled long block is not feasible. Instead, our solution combines:

*	a Short Block,
*	a complete Cylinder Head Assembly, and
*	the appropriate flywheel.

This configuration will allow end users to build a long block efficiently and cost‑effectively.
However, the success of this project depends heavily on competitive pricing. 

If we cannot reach a price level that convinces customers to choose a genuine Isuzu solution, the market will shift to non‑genuine alternatives very quickly.

 

4. Margin targets and market realities
The revised ISZE BP (4+8) sets margins at 34.6% for FY2026 and 33.5% for FY2027.
While we understand and support these targets, applying them strictly to short block pricing results in a final price that is not competitive in today’s market environment.
A more flexible SPA for BLOCK ASM and CRANKSHAFT will help us protect volume, defend our market share, and strengthen the long‑term business case for the new Industrial Long Block project.

This support was included in the business plan, following the way things were done at ISZE at the time — commit first, justify later. We fully understand your point that this is not the right approach, and we agree.

 

I have now completed a full study using all deals covered by this support, recalculated at our current 2026 prices. The numbers justify the programme:

 

  • Total sales generated (turnover):  €333,389

  • ISZE cost of goods:                €84,182

  • ISZE Gross Profit:                 €165,025  (~50% GP margin)

  • Return on €30K support:            ~5.5x in gross profit

 

Without DLOD, these deals would go to aftermarket suppliers and be lost entirely to ISZE.

 

Could you please confirm your approval to continue the programme at the current €30,000 cap?

 

More importantly, I want to commit to your way of working for all future support of this kind. Going forward, before any support is agreed or included in a business plan, we will:

1. Run a ROI study to validate the business case

2. Conduct a feasibility check with the distributor to agree scope and targets upfront

3. Request regular progress updates from the distributor throughout

 

This should have been the process from the start. It will be from here on.

 

Let me know if you'd like to discuss before signing off.

Dear Yoshimoto san,

 

ITUK operates in a competitive UK parts market where dealers regularly face pressure from aftermarket suppliers and second-hand parts. When the price gap is too wide, dealers lose the sale — and once a customer moves to aftermarket, they are very hard to recover. DLOD is a structured price support mechanism that allows ITUK to offer competitive pricing on a case-by-case basis, retaining customers on genuine Isuzu parts.

 

From ISZE's perspective, this is a direct revenue protection measure. Every part ITUK retains is a unit we sell upstream. Dear Yoshimoto san,

I checked with Duncan on the potential ROI, this is what he had said.

“From an ITUK perspective, the rationale for ISZE’s €10,000 contribution is not based on a direct or immediate financial return from the UK market alone, but rather on supporting a strategic initiative that strengthens genuine parts sales and retention for both ITUK and ultimately also ISZE.

The platform is designed to address future parts sales opportunities, for example targeting 3rd party repairers to claw back business currently going to factor parts suppliers like CV Components. A significant proportion of lost sales to the aftermarket is driven not by price, but by convenience and availability. By improving the ordering experience we expect to:

*	Increase order frequency from existing dealer and fleet customers
*	Improve retention of genuine parts by reducing leakage to factors
*	Provide a route to market for independent repairers who are currently outside of the network

 

In terms of financial return, while it is difficult to attribute a precise figure at this early stage, our expectation is that a relatively small uplift in parts sales will cover the €10,000 investment within a short period. Hi Jerome

 

From an ITUK perspective, the rationale for ISZE’s €10,000 contribution is not based on a direct or immediate financial return from the UK market alone, but rather on supporting a strategic initiative that strengthens genuine parts sales and retention for both ITUK and ultimately also ISZE.

The platform is designed to address future parts sales opportunities, for example targeting 3rd party repairers to claw back business currently going to factor parts suppliers like CV Components. A significant proportion of lost sales to the aftermarket is driven not by price, but by convenience and availability. By improving the ordering experience we expect to:

*	Increase order frequency from existing dealer and fleet customers
*	Improve retention of genuine parts by reducing leakage to factors
*	Provide a route to market for independent repairers who are currently outside of the network

 

In terms of financial return, while it is difficult to attribute a precise figure at this early stage, our expectation is that a relatively small uplift in parts sales will cover the €10,000 investment within a short period. For context, an increase of approximately 1–2% in annual parts turnover would be sufficient to offset this cost. If ITUK parts sales increase, so will ISZE parts sales increase.

We will closely monitor performance post-implementation and will be able to provide more concrete data on sales uplift, customer adoption, and ROI once the platform is fully live and embedded.

I hope this provides some clarity, but please let me know if you would like to discuss in more detail.

subject: RE: (note) almost SPA terminate at the end of Mar
body_preview:
Dear Suzuki-san,

 

Thank you very much for your message and for the detailed investigation.

 

It is correct that we currently maintain a healthy margin.
However, a price adjustment is strategically important for us at this stage, and I would like to outline the key business reasons behind this request.

 

1. Safeguarding sales volume for ageing Stage 3A machines
Most short block sales today are for Stage 3A models, which are approaching the later stages of their economic lifecycle. 

Owners of these machines are extremely cost‑sensitive. If the repair cost is too high, they often choose to scrap the machine rather than invest in an engine replacement.
In these cases, we lose not only the short block sale, but also future parts turnover for that machine.
Competitive pricing helps keep these units operational, which ultimately supports Isuzu’s long‑term installed base in Europe.

 

2. Preventing market loss to low‑cost alternatives
End users increasingly compare our prices with local remanufactured engines and complete overhauls built with cheap copy parts.
If our price gap becomes too wide, customers choose these alternatives, and we lose the entire opportunity.
By keeping short block pricing attractive, we retain the business within the Isuzu ecosystem, ensuring reliability, quality perception, and customer loyalty.

 

3. Strategic importance of the new Industrial Long Block project
We are preparing to launch a new Industrial Long Block concept.
Due to the many variations in flywheel housings, a fully assembled long block is not feasible. Instead, our solution combines:

*	a Short Block,
*	a complete Cylinder Head Assembly, and
*	the appropriate flywheel.

This configuration will allow end users to build a long block efficiently and cost‑effectively.
However, the success of this project depends heavily on competitive pricing. 

If we cannot reach a price level that convinces customers to choose a genuine Isuzu solution, the market will shift to non‑genuine alternatives very quickly.

 

4. Margin targets and market realities
The revised ISZE BP (4+8) sets margins at 34.6% for FY2026 and 33.5% for FY2027.
While we understand and support these targets, applying them strictly to short block pricing results in a final price that is not competitive in today’s market environment.
A more flexible SPA for BLOCK ASM and CRANKSHAFT will help us protect volume, defend our market share, and strengthen the long‑term business case for the new Industrial Long Block project.

 

 

I hope this explanation clarifies why maintaining the current SPA for BLOCK ASM and CRANKSHAFT is critical not only for immediate sales, but for sustaining Isuzu’s position in the European aftermarket and ensuring the success of future projects.

Please feel free to contact us if you need any additional information or further details.

 

 

Best regards,

Peter De Clercq

 

Isuzu Motors Europe will be closed on Friday 27 March, 2026.

Dear Suzuki‑san,

 

Thank you very much for your message below.

I kindly request your review of the SPA for the Short Block Project related to our local assembly activities.

 

The Short Block has become well established in the EU market, and sales continue to grow. It is highly valued as an alternative to expensive or unavailable complete engines. 

This solution allows older machines to remain operational, which in turn supports higher parts sales and strengthens customer retention.
For these reasons, we hope to continue with the SPA for this project in the same manner as before.

 

In the attached PDF, you will find:

*	The SPA request form and your current SPA list for the SB project
*	A summary of the cost and selling price, including our expected GM
*	ISZE sales history of locally assembled Short Blocks

 

I hope the request form has been completed to your satisfaction. If there is anything you would like me to modify, please let me know.

 

Please note that packaging costs (wooden crates and VCI foil) and transport costs to/from the assembly company are not included. 

These costs are small and distributed across multiple SB units per shipment, making precise allocation difficult. 

The overall impact is minimal and can reasonably be disregarded.

 

Key reasons to maintain the SPA

1.	HCME concerns regarding competitive fairness
	HCME has expressed concerns about “unfair” competition, as Isuzu distributors sell directly to the market while Hitachi dealers do not.
	To help address this pricing imbalance, we are in discussions with HCME and preparing a promotional campaign that will offer a 15% discount on both Short and Long Blocks.
2.	Risk of quality issues when workshops assemble Short Blocks themselves
	Some workshops with sufficient technical skills may choose to assemble a Short Block independently when they have idle technicians.
	In such cases, the final quality is not always guaranteed, which may jeopardize the Isuzu brand reputation.
	Ensuring that the complete Short Block is priced attractively will encourage workshops to choose the official solution instead of assembling their own.
3.	Practical limitations in Long Block production
	Due to the numerous variations in Flywheel Housings, producing a Long Block that fits a broad range of industrial engine models is not feasible.
	A more practical solution is to combine a Short Block with a complete HEAD ASM, the correct Flywheel Housing and Oil Pan, allowing customers to assemble the Long Block themselves.
	The complete HEAD ASM is currently under development and is expected to be available later this year.

body_preview:
Dear Saskia san

 

Thank you for your kind attention and communicate with Bosch HQ for their internal rules about ISUZU parts business.

According to your reports, Bosch HQ does not have any concerns to make some EU origin item local source.(Not sourced from Bosch Japan)

(ref. we have similar request in the US market. I heard that Bosch Japan mentioned that it should be all or nothing(in other word, INAC must procure all markets demand), but it seems not to meet your report/ Bosch internal rule)

 

Then if it could be clear at supplier issue, next it must set up how manage the operation (parts technical and service).

Could you please advise us how you think and manage the operation by making genuine parts local source.

1) ITC/supersede: ISZE daily update as the latest part number followed by parts master data (To my remember, that is the last time comments from ISZE) 

2) improvements parts: ISZE daily update as the latest part number followed by service bulletin (To my remember, that is the last time comments from ISZE) 

3) royalty: ISZE pays the certain ratio like 5% of DNP to ISZJ (To my remember, that is the last time comments from ISZE)

Dear Yoshimoto-san, 

Dear Masumi-san,

 

I wanted to bring the below to your attention before we respond to IIF Dubai.

 

We received a request from Nino Baluarte at IIF in Dubai, who is exploring an alternative shipping route from Europe directly to Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and North Africa, in response to current disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz affecting Middle East shipments.

 

In principle, I think we can be open to supporting this. However, before we commit to anything, there is one practical constraint we need to address: we would need to check with accounting whether all relevant African customers can be set up on our side to handle this flow correctly — invoicing, billing entities. Depending on how many customers are involved, this setup process could take some time.

 

My suggestion would be to reply to IIF positively but manage their expectations on timing. Obviously, I wanted your green light before we do so.

 

Please let me know if you have any concerns or a different view.
Please let me know if I need to ask certain questions to them.


Kind regards,

Subject: Alternative option Isuzu Europe to SSA dealers 

 

Dear Jerome-san, Bart-san,

 

Good day. My name is Nino Baluarte, and I currently handle inbound and outbound supply management from IIF  here in Dubai.

 

As of March 2026, the Middle East region is experiencing significant disruption due to ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical gateway for global shipping. As a result, shipments transiting this area are facing delays, especially those involving the Dubai, UAE.

 

In light of these challenges, shipping from Europe to Sub-Saharan Africa or North Africa is considered a viable alternative. However, this option may also come with certain limitations.

 

Given the current circumstances, we are carefully evaluating shipment priorities and considering Europe-to-SSA routing where feasible, particularly for cargo destined for African markets. This approach may help mitigate delays and reduce exposure to the ongoing disruptions in the Middle East.

 

Please let us know your thoughts on this plan and advise if there are any concerns or specific shipment requirements.

 

 

 

Thanks and Best regards, 

 

Nino Baluarte

Group Manager

Parts Operations Department



ISUZU MOTORS INTERNATIONAL FZE

body_preview:
Dear Yoshimoto-san, 

Dear Masumi-san,

 

I wanted to bring the below to your attention before we respond to IIF Dubai.

 

We received a request from Nino Baluarte at IIF in Dubai, who is exploring an alternative shipping route from Europe directly to Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and North Africa, in response to current disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz affecting Middle East shipments.

 

In principle, I think we can be open to supporting this. However, before we commit to anything, there is one practical constraint we need to address: we would need to check with accounting whether all relevant African customers can be set up on our side to handle this flow correctly — invoicing, billing entities. Depending on how many customers are involved, this setup process could take some time.

 

My suggestion would be to reply to IIF positively but manage their expectations on timing. Obviously, I wanted your green light before we do so.

 

Please let me know if you have any concerns or a different view.
Please let me know if I need to ask certain questions to them.


Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Subject: Alternative option Isuzu Europe to SSA dealers 

 

Dear Jerome-san, Bart-san,

 

Good day. My name is Nino Baluarte, and I currently handle inbound and outbound supply management from IIF  here in Dubai.

 

As of March 2026, the Middle East region is experiencing significant disruption due to ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical gateway for global shipping. As a result, shipments transiting this area are facing delays, especially those involving the Dubai, UAE.

 

In light of these challenges, shipping from Europe to Sub-Saharan Africa or North Africa is considered a viable alternative. However, this option may also come with certain limitations.

 

Given the current circumstances, we are carefully evaluating shipment priorities and considering Europe-to-SSA routing where feasible, particularly for cargo destined for African markets. This approach may help mitigate delays and reduce exposure to the ongoing disruptions in the Middle East.

Dear Yoshimoto san,

 

ITUK operates in a competitive UK parts market where dealers regularly face pressure from aftermarket suppliers and second-hand parts. When the price gap is too wide, dealers lose the sale — and once a customer moves to aftermarket, they are very hard to recover. DLOD is a structured price support mechanism that allows ITUK to offer competitive pricing on a case-by-case basis, retaining customers on genuine Isuzu parts.

 

From ISZE's perspective, this is a direct revenue protection measure. Every part ITUK retains is a unit we sell upstream. The €30,000 annual envelope is a fixed, controlled commitment to defend a revenue stream worth significantly more across the active UK parc. ITUK provides full deal activity records as evidence, giving us visibility into where genuine parts are price-uncompetitive in the market.

subject: Lubricant business - feasability check from accounting / finance perspective
body_preview:
Dear Gina,

I wanted to loop you in on a project we're working on around lubricants.

 

Isuzu HQ is exploring a centralised lubricant purchasing model where Isuzu Europe (ISZE) acts as the central purchasing entity, leveraging the Isuzu Group's global volume to access better supplier pricing than individual markets can achieve on their own. This is something we want to move forward on, and the commercial structure is taking shape.

 

On the commercial side, we're looking at three possible models (see attached slide):

- Alt 1: ISZE buys from the supplier and resells to distributors, handling both the commercial transaction and delivery

- Alt 2: Direct shipment where ISZE controls the commercial transaction but the supplier ships directly to distributors

- Alt 3: Commission scheme where ISZE acts as agent and the supplier deals directly with distributors

 

Before we go further, I need your input on two things:

 

1. What legal and contractual documents would be required to make this work — for each of the three models, we're potentially dealing with three different business entities (ISZE, the lubricant supplier, and the distributors). What would we need in place — MOUs, supply agreements, reseller contracts, agency agreements, intercompany arrangements?

 

2. Whether ISZE finance dept. can operationally support this — invoicing flows, intercompany billing, VAT implications across markets, and anything else we'd need to account for.

 

We're still in the assessment phase, so no decisions have been made yet. But I'd rather get your view early before we commit to a structure that creates problems downstream.

Many thanks for your input.





Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Subject: Olie project Isuzu

 

Beste Bavo

 

Als fabrikant evalueert Isuzu momenteel de integratie van de oliebusiness in onze algemene Europese bedrijfsstructuur.

 

Het doel van dit initiatief is tweeledig. 

Enerzijds willen we de kwaliteit van de oliën die binnen ons netwerk worden gebruikt verder optimaliseren. 

Anderzijds zien we duidelijke mogelijkheden om de omzet en winstmarges voor alle betrokken partijen te verhogen, 

terwijl tegelijkertijd de totale kosten worden verlaagd.

Dit zal gepaard gaan met de creatie van een nieuwe Isuzu-branded olie.

 

Deze aanpak is reeds succesvol geïmplementeerd in andere regio’s, waar ze zowel commercieel als operationeel tastbare voordelen heeft opgeleverd. 

Op basis van deze positieve ervaringen willen we nu ook onze Europese distributeurs betrekken bij het verkennen van gelijkaardige opportuniteiten.

 

Ons uitgangsprincipe binnen dit project is duidelijk: het doel moet altijd zijn om minstens dezelfde of vergelijkbare voordelen te behouden als vandaag -

of verbeterde voordelen te realiseren.  En dit steeds tegen een competitiever prijsniveau.

 

In deze fase benaderen we de grootste Europese markten om de eerste interesse te peilen.

Gelieve te noteren dat we op dit moment geen enkele verbintenis vragen. 

Het doel van deze communicatie is uitsluitend om te onderzoeken of er interesse is in een eerste gesprek om de huidige situatie in kaart te brengen, 

inclusief bestaande overeenkomsten, voordelen en specifieke noden.

 

Op basis van deze gesprekken kunnen we vervolgens evalueren of er bereidheid is om deel te nemen aan de volgende stap van het proces, 

wat in een latere fase mogelijk kan leiden tot betrokkenheid bij een prijstender.

 

Wij zouden het zeer op prijs stellen indien u ons laat weten of IBX openstaat voor een eerste gesprek over dit onderwerp.

 

Alvast bedankt voor uw overweging.

 

 

 

   Kind regards,

Koen Matheussen

Assistant Manager

Subject: Isuzu lubricant project

 

Dear John, Ben, Neil

 

As manufacturer, Isuzu is currently evaluating the integration of the lubricant business into our overall European business structure.

 

The objective of this initiative is twofold. On the one hand, we aim to further optimize the quality of the lubricants used across our network. 

On the other hand, we see clear potential to increase turnover and profit margins for all parties involved, while at the same time reducing overall costs.

This will be accompanied by the creation of a new Isuzu-branded oil.

 

This approach has already been successfully implemented in other regions, where it has delivered tangible benefits both commercially and operationally. 

Based on these positive experiences, we would now like to involve our European distributors in exploring similar opportunities.

 

Our guiding principle in this project is clear: the goal must always be to maintain at least the same or comparable 

advantages as today — or to achieve improved benefits. And this always at a more competitive price level.

 

At this stage, we are approaching the largest European markets to assess initial interest. 

Please note that we are not asking for any commitment at this moment. 

The purpose of this communication is solely to explore whether there is interest in an introductory discussion to map the current situation,

including existing agreements, benefits, and specific needs.

 

Based on these discussions, we can then evaluate whether there is a willingness to participate in the next step of the process, 

potentially leading to involvement in a price tender in a later stage.

 

We would highly appreciate your feedback by on whether you would be open to a first exchange on this topic.

Thank you in advance for your consideration.

 

 

   Kind regards,

Hi Koen,

Sorry for my late reply!

We have discussed this today and based on this our feedback to you are:


*	
	We have, as you know, a very good agreement with Total Energies
*	
	This agreement gives our different dealers:

	*	
		Easy access to "all the lubricants" they need - for all the brands they represent
	*	
		MyLubPortal for ordering
	*	
		Short delivery times
	*	
		Good prices
	*	
		Safety Data Sheet and other documentations needed for all products (ref the problems we have had with the missing safety data sheet related to art 5-87703001-00)
	*	
		Tecnical support


*	
	For RSA there are several advantages, but the three most important

	*	
		We don't need to have the products in stock (purchasing/storage/ safety data sheet and so on) and this is of course a cost effective solution
	*	
		We do not need to invest in "lubricants" knowledge
	*	
		We get a small volume based kick back from Total 


Based on this, we strongly belive that RSA and our dealers are better off with the solution we have today with Total Energies.

If you want to discuss this with us, - please feel free to contact us.

Some distributors are exceeding their original target or 4+8 target, but we don’t increase the incentive kickback amount for them.

Kin

Hi Yoshimoto san,

 

Attached you can find the overview of the targets for VP FY26.

Concerning your questions, please find feedback below:

 

・The targets and incentive amounts agreed with the distributor at the start of this period

>>> The original targets (see attached) and their corresponding yearly incentives have been communicated to the 10 distributors in this file. We also explained, they need to provide KPI feedback on regular basis, to be eligible for 100% of the incentive kickback amount (= 80% for sales + 20% for KPI)

・The targets and incentive amounts agreed with the distributor following the downward revision (9+3)

>>> The 9+3 targets (see attached) and their unchanged corresponding yearly incentives were communicated with the same conditions for the incentive kickback amount (= 80% for sales + 20% for KPI).

・Why it is necessary to change the incentive structure agreed at the start of the period

>>> 1)In the beginning of the FY26, some distributors gave feedback that the target ISZE had set to them for this FY was not achievable. In fact, some reacted almost angry with us. 

         2)IBX and ISD are still trying to catch up on reaching their targets, but due to the Astara IT platform issues, they could not place orders with us for many weeks in a row (April-May). They mentioned to us this is a big disadvantage for them. 

         3)We’re trying to motivate our distributors to reach at least 9+3 targets (if it is lower vs. 4+8 target), so we can secure the sales. 

 

Some distributors are exceeding their original target or 4+8 target, but we don’t increase the incentive kickback amount for them. 

We stick to what is budgeted for FY26. All kickbacks are already provisioned by Gina san.

 

Let us know if you would like to have an online call with us, or if this explanation is clear enough for you.

 

Kind regards,

Hadi

that covers 2 months of sales.

body_preview:
Dear Suzuki‑san,

 

Thank you very much for your message below.

I kindly request your review of the SPA for the Short Block Project related to our local assembly activities.

 

The Short Block has become well established in the EU market, and sales continue to grow. It is highly valued as an alternative to expensive or unavailable complete engines. 

This solution allows older machines to remain operational, which in turn supports higher parts sales and strengthens customer retention.
For these reasons, we hope to continue with the SPA for this project in the same manner as before.

 

In the attached PDF, you will find:

*	The SPA request form and your current SPA list for the SB project
*	A summary of the cost and selling price, including our expected GM
*	ISZE sales history of locally assembled Short Blocks

 

I hope the request form has been completed to your satisfaction. If there is anything you would like me to modify, please let me know.

 

Please note that packaging costs (wooden crates and VCI foil) and transport costs to/from the assembly company are not included. 

These costs are small and distributed across multiple SB units per shipment, making precise allocation difficult. 

The overall impact is minimal and can reasonably be disregarded.

 

Key reasons to maintain the SPA

1.	HCME concerns regarding competitive fairness
	HCME has expressed concerns about “unfair” competition, as Isuzu distributors sell directly to the market while Hitachi dealers do not.
	To help address this pricing imbalance, we are in discussions with HCME and preparing a promotional campaign that will offer a 15% discount on both Short and Long Blocks.
2.	Risk of quality issues when workshops assemble Short Blocks themselves
	Some workshops with sufficient technical skills may choose to assemble a Short Block independently when they have idle technicians.
	In such cases, the final quality is not always guaranteed, which may jeopardize the Isuzu brand reputation.
	Ensuring that the complete Short Block is priced attractively will encourage workshops to choose the official solution instead of assembling their own.
3.	Practical limitations in Long Block production
	Due to the numerous variations in Flywheel Housings, producing a Long Block that fits a broad range of industrial engine models is not feasible.
	A more practical solution is to combine a Short Block with a complete HEAD ASM, the correct Flywheel Housing and Oil Pan, allowing customers to assemble the Long Block themselves.
	The complete HEAD ASM is currently under development and is expected to be available later this year.

 

Please feel free to contact us if you need any further details or clarification.



We look forward to your feedback and appreciate your continued cooperation.

 

 

Best regards,

Hello Masumi,

 

Happy to clarify both points.

 

*ITUK UIO calculation through 2030*

 

The starting point is actual net registration data by model and vintage year, sourced from SMMT (the same underlying data Duncan's file uses). This gives us the number of vehicles registered in each year 

 

To convert registrations into UIO, I applied the CV Developed survival rate curve from IML Calculation.xlsx to each vintage cohort. For example, N75 units registered in 2016 (621 units) are still partially in service in 2025 at an estimated 70% survival rate, contributing 435 units to the 2025 UIO total. This is repeated across all models and all vintage cohorts, and summed for each projection year.

 

The model is then calibrated so that the 2024 output matches the known actual ITUK car park figure (N-series: 21,584 units; F-Series: 805 units).

 

Extending to 2030 requires no additional assumptions — the cohort decay model simply continues running on the existing registration data. Duncan's file stops at 2027 because of the assumptions he chose to apply, not because the underlying data runs out. A full worked example for N75 in 2025 is included in the file.

 

*LCV UIO projection through 2030*

 

You are correct that IMIT's LCV forecast only extends to FY2029. For CY2029 and CY2030, I applied a trailing CAGR per country as an extrapolation. This is an estimate, not a plan figure, and is flagged as such in the file.

body_preview:
Good morning, Koen

 

Here in the UK, we work with a partner called Morris Lubricants for all our various brand’s needs, some details as follows:

*	Our current suppliers receive all orders direct from our dealer network via a weblink sat on our Extranet. 
*	They have a helpdesk website that informs them which lubricant is required for which model by brand, see below:

 

“To find the correct oils & lubricants, enter a reg number for a car, classic car, motorbike, van, truck or HGV. Click the correct icon in the yellow box before entering a reg number. Or use the search bar and enter the make & model of a vehicle or machine. You can also select a product category and use the dropdown menus.”

 

*	Orders can range from bulk, barrels, Drums to a case of 12 x 1 litre cartons.
*	They manage delivery dates, queries, etc. and then deliver direct to the dealer’s premises.

	*	Note: We at IM, do not store lubricants in our warehouse

*	They then invoice IM for all dealer delivers made and then we invoice each dealer separately.

	*	Note: we see lubricants as a profit opportunity for the dealers rather than for IM.

*	They have their own blending operation, for new vehicle requirements and for technical investigations, which we can utilise for customer issues. 

 

As mentioned above, we will always be happy to review any programme that Isuzu launches. However, as we have a number of brands within our portfolio, any programme that we take would need to be able to satisfy the needs for all of them.

 

Should you have any further or more detail questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.
