Dear John

 

As manufacturer, Isuzu is currently evaluating the integration of the lubricant business into our overall European business structure.

 

The objective of this initiative is twofold. On the one hand, we aim to further optimize the quality of the lubricants used across our network. 

On the other hand, we see clear potential to increase turnover and profit margins for all parties involved, while at the same time reducing overall costs.

This will be accompanied by the creation of a new Isuzu-branded oil.

 

This approach has already been successfully implemented in other regions, where it has delivered tangible benefits both commercially and operationally. 

Based on these positive experiences, we would now like to involve our European distributors in exploring similar opportunities.

 

Our guiding principle in this project is clear: the goal must always be to maintain at least the same or comparable 

advantages as today — or to achieve improved benefits. And this always at a more competitive price level.

 

At this stage, we are approaching the largest European markets to assess initial interest. 

Please note that we are not asking for any commitment at this moment. 

The purpose of this communication is solely to explore whether there is interest in an introductory discussion to map the current situation,

including existing agreements, benefits, and specific needs.

 

Based on these discussions, we can then evaluate whether there is a willingness to participate in the next step of the process, 

potentially leading to involvement in a price tender in a later stage.

Dag Bavo

 

Op dit moment zien we dat jullie totale aankopen voor FY 2026 (vandaag geüpdatet) €2.016.000 hebben bereikt, terwijl het target €2.390.000 bedraagt.

Dit betekent dat er nog €374.000 nodig is om het target te bereiken.

 

Daarnaast is ISZE, rekening houdend met de ontwikkelingen op de Europese markt en specifiek met de black-outperiode die verband houdt met jullie systeemwissel, uitzonderlijk bereid 

om de overeengekomen bonus reeds toe te kennen vanaf een omzet van €2.221.700.

Dit betekent dat er nog slechts €205.700 ontbreekt.

 

Wij willen jullie graag aanmoedigen om de resterende orders te plaatsen vóór 26 maart.

Op die manier kan dit bedrag tijdig gefactureerd worden, zodat het target nog kan worden behaald en jullie in aanmerking blijven komen voor de bonus van €28.000.

 

Gelieve er ook rekening mee te houden dat 80% van deze bonus rechtstreeks gekoppeld is aan het behalen van het aankoopdoel, 

terwijl de overige 20% wordt toegekend op voorwaarde dat de KPI-rapporten volledig en tijdig worden ingediend.

 

Indien er iets is waarbij wij jullie kunnen ondersteunen om het target te bereiken, laat het ons gerust weten.

Dank voor de goede samenwerking en we kijken ernaar uit om deze maand samen succesvol af te sluiten.

Op dit moment zien we dat jullie totale aankopen voor FY 2026 (vandaag geüpdatet) €2.016.000 hebben bereikt, terwijl het target €2.390.000 bedraagt.

Dit betekent dat er nog €374.000 nodig is om het target te bereiken.

Ik dacht dat de regel was dat budget execution enkel Masumi was.

Dat de budget execution diend ondersteund te worden door een MOU, was naast mezelf, Hadi en vermoedelijke ook Masumi tevens onwetend dat dan de MOU diende ondertekende te worden door MD. Dus Masumi heeft deze zonder verdere vragen ondertekend.
Bijgevold was ik dan onwetend dan de CN ook diende afgetekend te worden, want dit is het gevolg van de budget execution, die op dat moment reeds was ondertekend.

Dit om te voorkomen wanneer alles voldaan is om dan te berichten dat het fout is gebeurt.

Wat nu....moet nu een bijkomende budget execution aanvraag en MOU opgemaakt  worden, ondertekend door MD, alsook de reeds opgemaakte CN te laten onderteken door MD.

body_preview:
Dear All,

 

We receive the news that there are strikes in harbours as Zeebruges, Ghent, Antwerp and also outside Belgian harbours.

The action is spread in the entire nautical chain (traffic control, pilots and maritime services) and is linked to federal pension reforms.
As there is a national strike scheduled in BE for the 12th of March, the disruption will continue until (at least) Thursday evening.
Recovery of this action may take several days due to the backlog.

 

The good news for ISZE for this week, is that the inbound containers scheduled to be delivered will be delivered at our warehouse, because they are already at TCT.

If the actions continue after Thursday 12.03.2026, we will update you again.

Dear Jerome, Dear Hadi,

As  Eran already mentioned, the recent price update places us in a very challenging position in front of our market.

Please bear in mind that since these trucks are used for commercial operations, the market tends to find alternative and more cost-effective solutions very quickly.

Therefore, and considering that you mentioned that “the price increase itself won’t be reversed,” we would appreciate your urgent assistance in setting up the SPA package still this month.

Please let us know if you encounter any issues with our quotations.

I am confident you will do your best to support us. Could you please advise when we may expect to receive your proposal?

Best regards,

Thanks

Yossi.

נושא: RE: Price file 2026

 

Dear Eran,

Thanks for your email and for sending over those examples. 
We hear you — particularly on the high-volume parts where aftermarket competition and parallel imports are a real pressure.

We'll go through the items you flagged and loop in management on your feedback.

To give you some context: the 2026 revision followed our annual supplier update and the weighted pricing logic we apply across the range. 
Worth noting that over the past 26.5 months, our prices went up by around 2% in total — so while I understand this adjustment feels sharp, the cumulative picture is fairly modest.

The price increase itself won't be reversed. That said, we genuinely want to work with you to protect genuine parts sales, not against you.



Two things I'd like to follow up on specifically. 
First, parallel imports — this is something we want to tackle more seriously, and it would really help to know where you think the parts are coming from. Any intel you can share would be useful. 

Second, the SPAs — I know you've been waiting on this longer than you should have.
I still need to sit down with our MD, and the past few weeks got away from us with fiscal year closing. It's not forgotten, and we want to move forward.

We'll come back to you once we've had a chance to review internally.

 

 

Best regards,

 

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Dear Eran,

Thanks for your email and for sending over those examples. 
We hear you — particularly on the high-volume parts where aftermarket competition and parallel imports are a real pressure.

We'll go through the items you flagged and loop in management on your feedback.



To give you some context: the 2026 revision followed our annual supplier update and the weighted pricing logic we apply across the range. 
Worth noting that over the past 26.5 months, our prices went up by around 2% in total — so while I understand this adjustment feels sharp, the cumulative picture is fairly modest.

The price increase itself won't be reversed. That said, we genuinely want to work with you to protect genuine parts sales, not against you.




Two things I'd like to follow up on specifically. 
First, parallel imports — this is something we want to tackle more seriously, and it would really help to know where you think the parts are coming from. Any intel you can share would be useful. 

Second, the SPAs — I know you've been waiting on this longer than you should have.
I still need to sit down with our MD, and the past few weeks got away from us with fiscal year closing. It's not forgotten, and we want to move forward.

We'll come back to you once we've had a chance to review internally.

 

 

Best regards,

Hi Gina

 

Ik dacht dat de regel was dat budget execution enkel Masumi was.
Dit staat zo weergegeven in de budget template document.



 

Dat de budget execution diend ondersteund te worden door een MOU, was naast mezelf, Hadi en vermoedelijke ook Masumi tevens onwetend dat dan de MOU diende ondertekende te worden door MD. Dus Masumi heeft deze zonder verdere vragen ondertekend.
Bijgevold was ik dan onwetend dan de CN ook diende afgetekend te worden, want dit is het gevolg van de budget execution, die op dat moment reeds was ondertekend.

De MOU werd doorgestuurd naar Finance Accounting op 9 februari, en tot u bericht was geen info gedeeld dat Masumi signature onvoldoende was.
Noch werd gesproken op 9 februari over de regel dat de CN diende ondertekend te worden door MD.


De CN werd opgemaakt op 4 maart, je kan er niet om omheen dat er voldoende tijd was om mezelf, (en sales en Hadi) te berichten dat hoewel budget execution niet door MD dient afgetekend te worden, alle ondersteunde documenten zijnde MOU en CN wel door MD dienen ondertekend te worden. 
Dit om te voorkomen wanneer alles voldaan is om dan te berichten dat het fout is gebeurt.

Wat nu....moet nu een bijkomende budget execution aanvraag en MOU opgemaakt  worden, ondertekend door MD, alsook de reeds opgemaakte CN te laten onderteken door MD.
Of mogen de huidige documenten behouden blijven? En ernkel de opgemaakt CN te laten ondertekenen door MH of door MH en MD.



Dank bij voorbaat voor je advies

 

Bijkomend:
Om verwarring te vermijden in de toekomst, mag ik dan vragen dat de budget template document aangepast wordt, zie vb hieronder.
Although MD signature for Budget execution is not needed, all supporting documents to be signed by MD (MOU & CN).



Alvast dank om de mogelijkheid te bekijken


Met vriendelijke groeten

 

Dirk

body_preview:
Hi Jerome,

 

 

Regarding the P700 R&M program, progress is currently slightly slow due to several ongoing topics.

 

One of the main points concerns the implementation of service intervals in the instrument cluster. At the time, there were still uncertainties from Isuzu, and this topic will likely only be resolved in the next generation (VK05).

 

We are also still discussing with Service in Japan, including for the F-Series, regarding the maintenance parts recommended by R&D. This has an impact on the R&M cost calculations, particularly when considering potential warranty costs.

 

Additionally, the figures currently available are mainly based on the previous model. In some cases, customers were also able to purchase the maintenance package before the first maintenance service, not only at the time of vehicle purchase.

I also expect a temporary decline in some R&M KPIs due to the period during which vehicle availability was limited.

 

 

 

For the D-Max, the recent change of maintenance intervals for the new 2.2 engine from 20,000 km to 15,000 km requires reprogramming the vehicles and updating the R&M cost calculations, which is delaying the planned ramp-up.

We are already proposing the updated program to some fleet customers, but the presentation to the network is slightly delayed again for the new D-Max 2.2.

 

 



 

 

 

 

 

Cumprimentos

We have added Incentive amount in Z2SDB25 table which you can maintain via SM30.
Then we made 'Incentive Amount to Post' in Z2SDAB46 as not editable anymore so it's display only.
The logic for this field is now:
  - If rate is maintained, calculate Z2SDB25-TARGET * Z2SDB25-RATE
  - If rate is 0, assign Z2SDB25-INCENTIVE

Hallo Jimmy,

 

How can we fix  the following:

 

Adjustment for the amount Credit Note to generate = Incentive Amount to Post, would/should only be accessible / possible for myself and for Gina.

We agreed on this earlier in the project. 

 

We can indeed adjust the Incentive Amount to Post via Z2SDB26 (see my earlier screenshot) – but saving is needed, 

as we (Gina & myself) are not allowed (and are not able to) to  make the CN and sales is not allowed to adjust CN amounts)

 

Solution proposals – Thinking out loud: 

 

* As guidance told us that we need to update the Incentive Amount to Post, via Z2SDB26 => can you make it possible to save it for Gina & myself?

* Or add the field ‘Incentive Amoun to Post’ in SM30 Table Z2SDB26, so Gina or I can fill it in and it will be visible (not adjustable) in Z2SDB26.

   Like this it has not to be adjustable in Z2SDB46 if saving possibility in Z2SDB46 is not option for Gina and myself.

* Or add the field ‘Incentive Amount to Post’ in SM30 Table Z2SDB25, so Gina or I can fill it in and it will be visible (not adjustable) in Z2SDB26.

   This manual input is needed for all incentive types, which do not have any rating in it, with or without sales target (and they do exist a lot, as I took examples of Incentives of past 2 years)

Hello Eran,

I hope you are fine.

As manufacturer, Isuzu is currently evaluating the integration of the lubricant business into our overall European business structure.

 

The objective of this initiative is twofold. On the one hand, we aim to further optimize the quality of the lubricants used across our network. 

On the other hand, we see clear potential to increase turnover and profit margins for all parties involved, while at the same time reducing overall costs.

This will be accompanied by the creation of a new Isuzu-branded oil.

 

This approach has already been successfully implemented in other regions, where it has delivered tangible benefits both commercially and operationally. 

Based on these positive experiences, we would now like to involve our European distributors in exploring similar opportunities.

 

Our guiding principle in this project is clear: the goal must always be to maintain at least the same or comparable 

advantages as today — or to achieve improved benefits. And this always at a more competitive price level.

 

At this stage, we are approaching the largest European markets + Israel to assess initial interest. 

Please note that we are not asking for any commitment at this moment. 

The purpose of this communication is solely to explore whether there is interest in an introductory discussion to map the current situation,

including existing agreements, benefits, and specific needs.

 

Based on these discussions, we can then evaluate whether there is a willingness to participate in the next step of the process, 

potentially leading to involvement in a price tender in a later stage.

 

Kind regards,

body_preview:
Beste Bavo

 

Als fabrikant evalueert Isuzu momenteel de integratie van de oliebusiness in onze algemene Europese bedrijfsstructuur.

 

Het doel van dit initiatief is tweeledig. 

Enerzijds willen we de kwaliteit van de oliën die binnen ons netwerk worden gebruikt verder optimaliseren. 

Anderzijds zien we duidelijke mogelijkheden om de omzet en winstmarges voor alle betrokken partijen te verhogen, 

terwijl tegelijkertijd de totale kosten worden verlaagd.

Dit zal gepaard gaan met de creatie van een nieuwe Isuzu-branded olie.

 

Deze aanpak is reeds succesvol geïmplementeerd in andere regio’s, waar ze zowel commercieel als operationeel tastbare voordelen heeft opgeleverd. 

Op basis van deze positieve ervaringen willen we nu ook onze Europese distributeurs betrekken bij het verkennen van gelijkaardige opportuniteiten.

 

Ons uitgangsprincipe binnen dit project is duidelijk: het doel moet altijd zijn om minstens dezelfde of vergelijkbare voordelen te behouden als vandaag -

of verbeterde voordelen te realiseren.  En dit steeds tegen een competitiever prijsniveau.

 

In deze fase benaderen we de grootste Europese markten om de eerste interesse te peilen.

Gelieve te noteren dat we op dit moment geen enkele verbintenis vragen. 

Het doel van deze communicatie is uitsluitend om te onderzoeken of er interesse is in een eerste gesprek om de huidige situatie in kaart te brengen, 

inclusief bestaande overeenkomsten, voordelen en specifieke noden.

 

Op basis van deze gesprekken kunnen we vervolgens evalueren of er bereidheid is om deel te nemen aan de volgende stap van het proces, 

wat in een latere fase mogelijk kan leiden tot betrokkenheid bij een prijstender.

 

Wij zouden het zeer op prijs stellen indien u ons laat weten of IBX openstaat voor een eerste gesprek over dit onderwerp.

 

Alvast bedankt voor uw overweging.

 

 

 

   Kind regards,

	Posting period, the one that corresponds of the current month.
	 
	Reversal reason 02 should NOT be used – posting date will always be date you do the reversal = the date the CN is made.

Subject: RE: Lubricant business

 

Dear Yoshimoto san,

The gross margin on the lubricant business is approximately 20,79%, which is lower than our parts business where the average GM is around 40%. However, lubricants are a highly competitive product category, and profitability is primarily driven by volume rather than margin percentage.

Historically, this has been a complementary side business that provides ISZE with additional profit while supporting the overall business relationship with UMI. For example, the lubricant business generated approximately €92,000 of gross profit last year.

It is also important to note that the cost structure of the lubricant business is fundamentally different from the parts business.

Unlike parts:

*	Inbound transport costs are already included in the Shell purchase price, so ISZE does not bear additional freight costs.
*	Outbound costs are for UMI determined by the incoterms
*	Warehouse handling costs are minimal, as the lubricants are delivered directly to the outbound area and shipped out again.
*	There is no picking, shelving, quality inspection, or repacking process, which normally generates handling costs for parts, or storage costs which account for most of the warehouse costs.

As a result, the operational cost associated with this business is very limited, making the lubricant business an efficient way to generate additional contribution with minimal operational effort.

Kind regards,

Subject: RE: Lubricant business

 

Dear Yoshimoto san,



The gross margin on the lubricant business is approximately 20,79%, which is lower than our parts business where the average GM is around 40%. However, lubricants are a highly competitive product category, and profitability is primarily driven by volume rather than margin percentage.

Historically, this has been a complementary side business that provides ISZE with additional profit while supporting the overall business relationship with UMI. For example, the lubricant business generated approximately €92,000 of gross profit last year.

It is also important to note that the cost structure of the lubricant business is fundamentally different from the parts business.

Unlike parts:

*	Inbound transport costs are already included in the Shell purchase price, so ISZE does not bear additional freight costs.
*	Outbound costs are for UMI determined by the incoterms
*	Warehouse handling costs are minimal, as the lubricants are delivered directly to the outbound area and shipped out again.
*	There is no picking, shelving, quality inspection, or repacking process, which normally generates handling costs for parts, or storage costs which account for most of the warehouse costs.

As a result, the operational cost associated with this business is very limited, making the lubricant business an efficient way to generate additional contribution with minimal operational effort.

Let me share you with more detail.

 

Firstly, UIO calculation method for LCV is same as that used for CV. However, the survival ratio differs. LCV UIO is calculated for up to 12 years only, while CV are 15 or 20 years.

Please refer to the percentages applied in the sheet titled “Survival Ratio.” The LCV survival ratio is based on data from the Thai market.

 

Then, vehicle data, I have shared the sheet “RAW Data” The details are as follows:

1.	From 2003 to 2025 (B-X): Actual vehicle unit shipment data from Thailand
2.	From 2026 onward (Y-AA): Estimated vehicle forecasts shared by IMIT vehicle team and each DLR. (Business plan at a time of request)

 

After receiving the vehicle data of each DLR, I simply paste the data into the “CALCULATION (12yr UIO)” sheet, in Row 2.

The file will then automatically calculate the UIO for each DLR, which can be found in Row 40.

 

Please note that  vehicle data is based on shipment dates from Thailand, not on retail sales at destination.

We started making some calculations for the genuine parts share project for this fiscal year.

Target: £12,690,000

subject: RE: inquiry for purchase order result and forecast gap in Feb
body_preview:
Dear Suzuki san,

 

Many thanks for your explanation, understood.

 

To get back to your question, no it is not our intention to lower our inventory level. Our current MoS is quite high indeed, but we have to take into account that we have received many initial orders, both on CV as LCV side. If all goes well, and the recommendation lists were accountable, the demand should pick up for these items soon and lower MoS levels again. 

On the other hand, we are always cautious not to overstock items as well. What I meant by the impact of the overdue ordered items is the fact that the transit lead times are coming back to normal, after the upwards deviations we experienced from IML over the summer. The transit LT is a key factor in the safety stock calculation. If it goes up (due to overdue order lines), the inventory level proposal, and therefore, our total commitments will be higher...once it goes down again, the order proposal will be lower again as less safety stock is needed.

 

On the other hand, it is better to monitor the MoS based on our stock on hand level. The MoS based on our TTL stock (includes stock in transit) also includes a large portion of PRD orders which are not taken into stock as they are directly linked to a customer order. Our current MoS target is 6.9, I will keep you posted if our management would like to revise this in the new FY.

 

Let me know if you have additional questions.

 

Kind regards,

Bart

 

Bart Van den Bosch

Parts Planning & Inventory Control | ISZE

December & January results

For December, the result was broadly in line with CV order intake.

For January, the result was slightly lower than expected but closer to target as shown in the ISZE system. ITUK orders

As explained in our report, ITUK was one of the key drivers this month, with €768k in stock orders, effectively doubling year‑on‑year. A portion (ordered in the last week of Feb) will only reflect in March stock orders.

 

Please let me know if anything remains unclear after the report distribution, and I will be happy to clarify.

 

Kind regards,

Bart

Dear all,

 

As we are currently implementing Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central (BC) together with ELVA DMS, and further digitalising our operations, we require structured, electronic access to both parts and service-related data. 

This request is directly linked to ensuring a successful and efficient system implementation.

To optimise the implementation and secure correct system setup from the outset, we need reliable, automated data access rather than manual reports or portal-based lookups. 

Below is a consolidated overview of the information we would need to access electronically, preferably via API, web services, EDI, or another automated integration method.


1. Spare Parts Data


Inventory & Availability (real-time or near real-time)


*       Current on-hand stock levels

*       Available-to-promise quantities

*       Incoming shipments and expected delivery dates


Open Orders & Back Order Status


*       List of open purchase orders

*       Ordered quantities

*       Confirmed delivery dates

*       Back order status

*       If a part is on back order: Estimated Time of Delivery (ETD)


Complete Parts Master Data


*       Part numbers (internal and supplier references)

*       Descriptions and technical specifications

*       Lead times and minimum order quantities (MOQ)

*       Packaging details

*       Country of origin and HS codes

*       Master data updates and effective dates


Product References, Supersession & Substitution


*       Cross-references between part numbers

*       Item supersession references (old-to-new and new-to-old links)

*       Superseded / replacement part numbers

*       Effective dates of supersession changes

*       Interchangeability rules and substitution logic

Full visibility into item supersession and substitution chains is critical to prevent ordering obsolete parts and to ensure correct replacement handling in our systems.


2. Service & Labour Data


In addition to parts data, we also require electronic access to vehicle service-related information.


Service & Labour Information


*       Flat rate times (standard repair times)

*       Service packages (including included parts and labour structure)

*       Official service schedules / maintenance programs

*       Labour master data (labour codes, descriptions, categories, warranty coding, etc.)

This information must be accessible via web services / API or another structured integration method so it can be integrated directly into our internal systems.

 

We look forward to your feedback and to aligning on a sustainable technical solution.

subject: Management announcement: compliments Day - opportunity to say thank you
body_preview:
Dear colleagues,

 

Sunday is Compliments Day — the perfect moment to officially hand out extra kudos. And honestly… you still make our job in HR incredibly enjoyable. 

 

We often notice that it’s simply assumed that everyone does what is expected of them (or even goes that little bit further). 

But that doesn’t mean we should give fewer compliments. On the contrary — we should probably say it a lot more often.

So here it is — because today it’s allowed and well‑deserved: you are all fantastic colleagues, one by one.

 

Thank you for your commitment, flexibility, humor, and teamwork. 

You are the reason our organization keeps running smoothly — not just because of what you do, but because of the way you do it: with dedication, cooperation, and genuine care. 

Every day, you make us proud. Please continue being who you are: professional when needed, delightfully chaotic when allowed, and always with your heart in the right place.

 

Happy Compliments Day! 💛

We wish you a wonderful (sunny) weekend,
Management & HR

 

 

Beste collega’s,

 

Zondag is het Complimentendag — dé dag waarop we officieel extra veel pluimpjes mogen uitdelen. En eerlijk… jullie maken het ons als HR nog altijd ongelooflijk plezant.

 

We merken vaak dat er gewoonweg van uitgegaan wordt dat iedereen doet wat van hem of haar verwacht wordt (of zelfs dat tikkeltje meer). 

Maar dat betekent niet dat we minder complimenten moeten geven. Integendeel: we zouden het eigenlijk wat vaker mogen zeggen.

Dus bij deze — omdat het officieel mag én verdiend is: jullie zijn één voor één topcollega’s.

 

Bedankt voor jullie inzet, flexibiliteit, humor en teamwork.

Jij bent de reden waarom onze organisatie zo goed draait – niet alleen vanwege wat je doet, maar ook vanwege de manier waarop je dat doen: met toewijding, samenwerking en oprechte zorg. 

Elke dag maak je ons trots. Blijf vooral zoals je bent: professioneel wanneer het moet, licht chaotisch wanneer het mag, en altijd met het hart op de juiste plek.

 

Fijne Complimentendag! 💛

 

We wensen jullie een fijn (zonnig), weekend,

Management & HR

The difference between the two fields is that the Sales amount to date gets cleared when you already create the incentive credit note. Jimmy

Subject: RE: Survey on EV battery scrapping / recycling

 

Hi Koen, 

 

With regard to the applicability of the EU Battery Regulation (Regulation EU: 2023/1542 - EUBR) in Iceland, please allow us to clarify the legal framework.

 

Iceland is not a member of the European Union. However, Iceland participates in the EEA through EFTA. EU legislation does not automatically apply in Iceland. 

For an EU regulation to become legally binding, it must first be formally incorporated into the EEA Agreement by decision of the EEA Joint Committee and subsequently implemented into Icelandic law where required.

 

As of now, the new EU Battery Regulation has not yet been formally incorporated into the EEA Agreement and therefore does not currently have legal force in Iceland.

Accordingly:

*	Legal compliance in Iceland is presently governed by existing national legislation on waste management, batteries, and extended producer responsibility, which is based on previously incorporated EU directives.
*	Compliance with EUBR is not yet a legal requirement in Iceland; however, alignment with its provisions may be considered prudent from a forward-looking and OEM harmonization perspective, as incorporation into the EEA framework is expected in due course.

 

Regarding your second question, and subject to full confidentiality between Isuzu and BL, we are able to share the document below of an older contract of non-commercial framework information relevant for benchmarking purposes.

 

Currently, BL has an active and formal agreement with one of the two major recycling companies operating in Iceland, Efnarás. This agreement governs the collection, handling, treatment, reporting, and regulatory compliance of end-of-life batteries in accordance with Icelandic environmental and waste legislation.

In parallel, we are evaluating an alternative recycling partner, Terra, with the intention that they may assume responsibility for handling lithium-ion batteries and other batteries like the 12V for BL going forward.

The primary drivers for this potential transition are:

*	Cost efficiency, as Terra offers a more competitive commercial structure.
*	Operational efficiency, as Terra does not require full dismantling of battery packs prior to recycling, thereby reducing handling complexity, labor exposure, and associated technical risk.

 

Any final decision will, of course, ensure full regulatory compliance and alignment with producer responsibility obligations in Iceland.

 

Again, this is sent in full confidentiality, and we ask you to handle this information with caution.

body_preview:
Hi Koen, 

 

With regard to the applicability of the EU Battery Regulation (Regulation EU: 2023/1542 - EUBR) in Iceland, please allow us to clarify the legal framework.

 

Iceland is not a member of the European Union. However, Iceland participates in the EEA through EFTA. EU legislation does not automatically apply in Iceland. 

For an EU regulation to become legally binding, it must first be formally incorporated into the EEA Agreement by decision of the EEA Joint Committee and subsequently implemented into Icelandic law where required.

 

As of now, the new EU Battery Regulation has not yet been formally incorporated into the EEA Agreement and therefore does not currently have legal force in Iceland.

Accordingly:

*	Legal compliance in Iceland is presently governed by existing national legislation on waste management, batteries, and extended producer responsibility, which is based on previously incorporated EU directives.
*	Compliance with EUBR is not yet a legal requirement in Iceland; however, alignment with its provisions may be considered prudent from a forward-looking and OEM harmonization perspective, as incorporation into the EEA framework is expected in due course.

 

Regarding your second question, and subject to full confidentiality between Isuzu and BL, we are able to share the document below of an older contract of non-commercial framework information relevant for benchmarking purposes.

 

Currently, BL has an active and formal agreement with one of the two major recycling companies operating in Iceland, Efnarás. This agreement governs the collection, handling, treatment, reporting, and regulatory compliance of end-of-life batteries in accordance with Icelandic environmental and waste legislation.

In parallel, we are evaluating an alternative recycling partner, Terra, with the intention that they may assume responsibility for handling lithium-ion batteries and other batteries like the 12V for BL going forward.

The primary drivers for this potential transition are:

*	Cost efficiency, as Terra offers a more competitive commercial structure.
*	Operational efficiency, as Terra does not require full dismantling of battery packs prior to recycling, thereby reducing handling complexity, labor exposure, and associated technical risk.

 

Any final decision will, of course, ensure full regulatory compliance and alignment with producer responsibility obligations in Iceland.

 

Again, this is sent in full confidentiality, and we ask you to handle this information with caution.

Hi Koen,

 

Once again reviewing the pricing for EV parts, I have performed an exercise comparing the new EV parts prices to the previous model parts pricing, I have highlighted a few part numbers where there has been a significant increase in cost for what appears to be the same part.

 

Could you please advise what the difference is to justify the increase in cost or push the factory to lower price so we can align them with the current parts on offer for current/previous model D-Max?

 

Rear axle case – 7553068050, EUR 2,640.76

 



 

As you can see the difference here is very large, I can see by the EPC that there is a difference between the current axle case and the new one for EV but the increase in price cannot be justified from our point to our network.

 

Cab Harness – 7552502532, EUR 1,897.26

 



 

Another situation where there has been a very large increase in price, this time however it is difficult to see the difference between the new EV part and current ICE part numbers.

 

Meter cluster – 7552482420, EUR 872.37

 



 

We understand there will be some variation in price due to the different types of display and spec of the vehicle but the EV cluster is more than double the price of the most expensive current ICE part number.

 

As always we appreciate you working with us on these issues and we just want to make sure that if the price is significantly more that we can justify this to our dealers and customers.

Dear Nadine,

For points 1 and 2, the provision amount displayed in the report is NOT the provision amount that's already posted, but rather it is the calculation of how much provision will be posted for every provision document. 
For example :
cust 90 - 2 MONTH INCENTIVE - Custom provision frequency
Provision amount in report = Total provision(240) / no. of periods(2) = 120
 
cust 90 - TRIP INCENTIVE - Monthly provision frequency
Provision amount in report = Total provision(2000) / no of periods(12) = 166.67

Hello Duncan,

I hope you are fine.

We started making some calculations for the genuine parts share project for this fiscal year.

 

For the spend per unit data as margin assumptions we used the calculations from Yoshimoto san. ( see attached ppt presentation )



As you know this is the first time, we do this exercise which reflects in the high Genuine pars share percentage.
Hopefully if we receive new data we can refine this model.

 

For the ISZE -> ITUK part we want to add 1% as an incentive increase of the genuine parts share for this fiscal year.
This would reflect in an additional purchase amount of  65.520€ before the end of this fiscal year.

 

If ITUK achieves this target, ISZE Sales intends to provide an incentive of €13,000. 
Please note that this incentive remains subject to final approval by our higher management.


Regarding the ITUK → Dealer Genuine Parts Share, we performed the same exercise. 
Based on the current figures, ITUK is not on track to reach the existing target. Therefore, setting a higher target this year does not seem realistic, unless there are inaccuracies in my calculations.

Actual result as of January: £10,274,044
Target: £12,690,000

 

 

Please let me know if you have any questions.

 

Kind regards,

 

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Hi, Hadi,

 

The figures shown in the screenshot are the YTD results – Apr 2025 through Jan 2026.
The Anaplan 10+2 is for the 12 months period, with 10 months’ actual results and 2 months’ forecast.

 

The question Yoshimoto san raised is whether we will achieve the gross profit target, given that we are likely miss the sales amount target at the fiscal year end.

 

As the GM calculation is based on SAP’s MAP cost (correct me if I am wrong), the impact of the recent purchase price increase will take effect gradually for the next couple of months. 

Looking at the VP and IE, the gross margins have evolved in somewhat differently over the fiscal term – VP shows an upward trend whereas IE downward.

That said, in both cases the YTD results are above the Anaplan 10+2 figures.

 

Ideally, ahead of H2 revision, we should take into account, and adopt to, the known variable factors in the coming months, such as purchase cost increase, ForEx differences, sales price increase.

I am not sure whether it is feasible to fully reflect these factors in the remaining two months.

Therefore, as mentioned in my previous mail, my suggestion is to simulate the end of March gross profit based on a defined run-rate.

Whichever approach you take, can you please document the logic behind the figures, so that we can explain the rationale and re-visit it in the future if needed?

 

Kind regards,

 

Masumi

MOU Overview

Summary:
MOU regarding the compensation amount from IMIT to ISZE for EV battery packs for LCVs (between IMIT and ISZE)

Scope:
Part No. 7552816560 (BATTERY ASM; HIGH VOLTAGE)

Term

From December 1, 2025 (retroactive), until termination or amendment by mutual agreement of both parties.

IMIT → ISZE Compensation

Overview and Billing Method:

*	Compensation amount: EUR 6,133 per unit
*	Timing of compensation:
	After ISZE sells to DB/DLR, ISZE will invoice based on the letter described below.
*	Billing method:
	ISZE issues a reimbursement letter and invoices IMIT (same operation as currently implemented between ISZE and IMIT).

Sales Price Conditions

*	IMIT → ISZE: EUR 38,409 per unit
*	ISZE → DB/DLR: EUR 38,794 per unit
*	Prices shall be maintained unless there is written agreement/consent from both parties.

 

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me at any time.

 

Thanks and regards,

 

Masumi

Subject: RE: Monthly parts sales plan for the next fiscal year

 

Dear Yoshimoto san,

 

The exchange rate validity period is fixed and applies either from 1 October 20## to 31 March 20##, or from 1 April 20## to 30 September 20##.

The applicable exchange rate is calculated by IML in accordance with the following methodology:

 

1.	Start from the current FX rate. 

	*	E.g. A : 153,3 JPY

2.	Define a ±5% tolerance band upwards and downwards.

	*	Downwards bound (B) : -5% : 145,6 JPY
	*	Upwards bound (C) : +5% : 161 JPY

3.	Calculate a 6‑month market average FX rate using TTM (monthly average from Refinitiv) data confirmed by IML Corporate Finance and Banking Relations Dept., E :

	Month

Ave. TTM

	Apr-2024

168,21

	May-2024

170,61

	Jun-2024

172,36

	Jul-2024

162,35

	Aug-2024

161,50

	Sept-2024

158,43

			
	6-Month Average 1 € = 

165,58

 

4.	Compare 6-Month Average against B and C:

	*	6-Month Average (E) >= Downwards bound (B) and  6-Month Average (E) <= Upwards bound  (C)

5.	Inside range → keep current FX rate
6.	Outside range → adjust
7.	Apply the adjustment logic to set New Applicable FX Rate

	*	If the 6‑month average FX rate stays within ±5% of the current rate, keep the current rate unchanged.
	*	If it moves outside that range, adjust the rate halfway toward the market average and round it to one decimal.

8.	Fix the rate for the defined applicable period.

 

Please see attached example accordingly. 

 

Kind regards,

Bart

 

Bart Van den Bosch

Parts Planning & Inventory Control | ISZE

	On Tue, 17 Feb 4:00 PM , Saskia wrote: 
	you can find more background in the attached email communication. 
	We have a new requirement for managing the supply of security parts, under the EU’s Repair and Maintenance Information (RMI) regulation.
	Under the regulation, the economic operator must conduct the customer verification, and keep the record of the sales. 
	
	
	We need to get the necessary information from the distributor, along with the VIN, when they order a key.
	We need to establish such a structure before the end of the year. 
	
	
	When a customer orders Security related parts (such as a remote key or an alarm system) our Sales team will need to receive an email or a notification of the order. this should trigger our Sales team to as the necessary information from the distributor who has placed the order.
	
	
	Is there a possibility to have such an email put in place? or is there a field in the Material Master we can fill in to trigger a warning or an email to the Sales team?
	We would need to know how we can control the orders and verify the order is correct by checking the information with our customer.

body_preview:
Dear all,

 

Duncan has shared the competitor pricing for brake pads – please see the attached excel file for reference.

This information was provided by one of his fleet customers and is particularly valuable.

 

A key comparison is with TRP Isuzu (cell H16), where DAF’s second-line range includes items that can fit to Isuzu.

Another important observation is the comparison with the genuine items of DAF and Iveco parts. Some customers may be reluctant to choose Isuzu for new or replacement vehicles due to the perceived higher cost of brake maintenance.

 

We should review whether current Isuzu BVP parts can be positioned more aggressively on price without eroding margin.

 

Please also note that the 7.5t vehicles fall under the UK Operators License (O-license) regulations, which require operators to carry out regular maintenance and inspections.

This regulatory requirement presents an opportunity to strengthen our parts offering and engagement with fleet customers.

 

Kind regards,

Masumi

Beste Bruno, beste Bavo, beste Roland

 

Hartelijk dank voor uw eerdere bestelling van onze BEV-voertuigen. Met deze stap positioneert IBX zich duidelijk in het snelgroeiende EV-segment, 

wat mooie commerciële opportuniteiten biedt in uw markt.

 

Om deze introductie maximaal te ondersteunen, willen wij het belang benadrukken van een adequate voorraad van de bijhorende EV-parts. 

Een snelle beschikbaarheid van kritische onderdelen is essentieel om uw klanten een professionele en betrouwbare service te bieden — 

zeker bij de introductie van nieuwe technologie zoals BEV.

 

Wij hebben u eerder de lijst met aanbevolen EV-parts bezorgd en voegen deze hierbij opnieuw toe ter referentie. 

Door deze onderdelen tijdig te bestellen, verzekert u niet alleen een vlotte aftersales-ondersteuning, maar versterkt u ook het vertrouwen

Dear Hadi,

 

We have a new (new to us…) requirement for managing the supply of security parts, under the EU’s Repair and Maintenance Information (RMI) regulation.

Under the regulation, the economic operator must conduct the customer verification, and keep the record of the sales.

 

Can we sit down together and discuss what/how we can do this?

 

What I understood is that we need build in the verification process, and the record-keeping system.

How to get the verification is via the agency called SERMI.

 

My guess is that we need to get this information from the distributor, along with the VIN, when they order the key.

 

We need to establish such a structure before the end of the year. Otherwise, the worst case is that we cannot get the type approval for any of our vehicles sold in the EU market.

 

 

Since we have not much time as some of you are receiving visitors and travelling for business this week,

I asked Copilot and got the following response:

 

Under EU Regulation 2018/858 and its Delegated Regulation 2021/1244, access to security-related vehicle parts and information is tightly controlled to balance repair market competition with vehicle cybersecurity. Here's a detailed breakdown:

 

🔐 What Are Security-Related Parts?

Security-related parts and functions include:

 

Anti-theft systems

Electronic immobilizers

Alarm systems

Remote keyless entry

Vehicle access control modules

Software and diagnostics related to these systems

These components are critical to preventing unauthorized access or theft, and therefore require controlled access for repair and maintenance.

 

🛠️ How Is Access Controlled?

1. SERMI Scheme (Security-Related RMI)

The SERMI (Security-related Repair and Maintenance Information) system is the EU-wide framework for managing access to security-related vehicle data.

 

Key Features:

Mandatory Accreditation: Independent operators (IOs) must be approved and authorized by a Conformity Assessment Body (CAB).

Employee Vetting: Technicians must be individually authorized.

Security Certificates: Access is granted only through secure, certified channels.

Non-discrimination: Once accredited, IOs must be treated equally to authorized dealers.

2. Regulatory Basis

Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1244 amends Annex X of Regulation 2018/858 to:

Define standardized access procedures.

Require compliance with ISO 18541 standards for RMI portals.

Establish Appendix 3, detailing the approval process for accessing security features.

🧩 Approval & Authorization Process

To access security-related RMI, independent operators must:

 

Apply to a CAB in their country.

Submit documentation proving legitimate business activity.

Undergo background checks (e.g., criminal record, insurance).

Receive SERMI certification.

Use secure tools and software compliant with ISO 18541.

Operators involved in activities like tampering with emissions systems or odometers are explicitly excluded from access.

 

🌍 Implementation Timeline

SERMI is being rolled out across EU countries in phases.

As of 2025, countries like Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Spain have active or upcoming SERMI implementations.

Dear Gina,

 

Allow me to explain why we work with this margin. As you know the Shell business is substantial for UMI (and VEH parts operations)

 


Here is a summary of how determined this pricing:

 

*	ISZE did not change their margin for these products since a few years.
*	We took a different approach for this product as the handling in our warehouse is different. It basically arrives & leaves as a whole shipment resulting in basically no handling & storage costs.
*	No transport costs, no duties are in place as well.
*	We also have reserved a support amount for the lubricant business 20K€. (Promotional support)
*	We used to work with a credit note from the Shell in the past, but Shell has proposed to reduced purchase prices for ISZE instead.

ISZE kept the CR to UMI as a safety measure to keep the required sales volume intact. (as you can see are margin increased to partially cover the credit note to UMI in combination with the promotional support amount)

 

I hope this explains the CR amount, please let me know if you still have questions.

 

AS UMI has now reached the target ISZE will reduce the sales price so no we don’t work with CR for the incoming shipments.

The attached file shows the above calculations, for your information.

 

Masumi

subject: RE: Inquiry for luburicant shipment to UK(ITUK/IUK)
body_preview:
Dear Suzuki san,

Please see the overview attached with all lubricants purchased by IUK / ITUK in CY2025, as requested.


IUK requires them on a separate invoice, reason is as follows:

 

IUK is not authorised to store excise goods (lubricants/oil) in its bonded warehouse.
If lubricants are included in standard consignments routed via Baxter Freight, the entire shipment must be cleared via a home-use customs entry, which immediately triggers excise duty and import VAT payment upfront.

Given the shipment size, this results in significant and unnecessary cash-out on duty and import charges.

Therefore:

*	Lubricants must be invoiced and shipped separately
*	They must not be included in bonded-warehouse consignments
*	This avoids forced home-use entry and protects IUK’s cash flow and customs compliance



Kind regards,

 

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Hello Masumi,

Sorry for my belated reply as last week we had IMIT , Koen was on business trip and this week I was ill.

 

I focused my self on the sales trend for the turnover side.
For the cost and gross margin side I focused myself on the MAP cost and thus the exchange rate & MOS levels to calculate how fast the FX rate would kick in.

Please see below the summary:  

1. Turnover development

*	Last 9 months turnover:
	€23.95m, equivalent to €2.66m per month (average)
*	Next 3 months projected turnover:
	€8.31m, equivalent to €2.77m per month

➡ This represents a ~4.1% increase in monthly run-rate turnover compared to the last 9 months.

 

2. Cost evolution (FX-adjusted, EUR)

*	Baseline cost for next 3 months (before FX):
	€4.52m
*	FX-adjusted cost (Month 3 run-rate):
	€4.42m
*	Cost reduction due to weaker JPY:
	≈ −2.3%, equivalent to ~€104k per 3-month period

 

Gross Margin impact

*	Baseline GM (next 3 months):
	€3.79m → GM%: 45.6%
*	FX-adjusted GM (Month 3 run-rate):
	€3.89m → GM%: 46.9%
*	GM uplift from FX alone:
	+€104k, corresponding to:

	*	+2.75% increase in absolute GM
	*	+1.25 percentage points GM% improvement

Hi, Hadi,

 

I have received a communication indicating that the IML parts dept has a consolidated sales target of 250 bil JPY, but no breakdown was provided.

I have now asked for the clarification on how this figure was derived and am currently awaiting their response.

 

Yoshimoto san and I have aligned on the overall direction, agreeing that we should apply the Isuzu IX growth rate (76% increase from FY2024).

As the results of FY2024 includes CL, I can see two approaches:

1.     Apply the growth rate to the total amount.

Multiply the FY2024 total by 1.76 top calculate the FY2031 target, then distribute the resulting amount across each business line and fiscal year.

2.	Apply the growth rate on each business line including CL.

Apply the increase separately to each business line, including CL, and then reallocate the CL portion to the remaining business lines.

This is somewhat simplistic, and results ion uneven year-on-year growth – FY2029 growth becomes disproportionately large compared to subsequent years.

You may wish to smooth out the growth trajectory so that it reflects a ore consistent annual increase, approximately 12% each year.

 

The attached file shows the above calculations, for your information.

 

Masumi

Hello Masumi,

 

 

Initially (in October 2025), I understood that we should work with ITUK sales-to-dealer data. As no guidance was given my thought was, if there is more specific data -> less assumptions -> more accurate result.

If you have a better approach or an alternative suggestion, I would very much appreciate your input.

 

Masumi

Based on our current tracking, this brings ITUK’s invoiced purchases to around €4.39m, compared to a full-year plan (including January) of €4.89m. This implies a remaining gap of roughly €0.5m with a good two months left in the period.

 

As PRD orders placed at this stage will not be invoiced within the current financial year, any catch-up would therefore need to come from SOR volumes.

Subject: RE: (ISZE) Request for the formulation of 9+3 and preparation for Kosha Hearing

 

Dear Masumi,

The key point in your request is the following:

 

 

“Prepare a list of PNs showing the differences in quantities, amounts and profit rates, and sorted in a way that highlights the variances.”

 

At present, we do not have a business plan or budget defined at part-number (PN) level. The planned figure ((Apr 24 – Mar 25) / 12 × 9) represents an aggregate financial plan, not a PN-based sales or margin plan. 
As a result, we can only provide is a direct PN-to-plan comparison with the same period the year before, but please keep in mind this would require the following assumptions:

 

A PN-level comparison can only be made against a historical period, not directly against the plan.

  Such a comparison does not isolate sales composition effects (model mix) from other drivers, including:

*	Warranty volume fluctuations
*	Seasonality (e.g. winter wear parts, summer service items)
*	Part lifecycle effects (e.g. declining RT parts, ageing vehicle parc)
*	Campaigns (which we did a lot last year)
*	Stock optimisation effects (stock rebalancing, a lot of DB’s adjust their MOS level due to various reasons)

 

Unless you advise otherwise, I will proceed with the analysis based on the same historical reference period.

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

body_preview:
Dear Masumi,

The key point in your request is the following:

 

 

“Prepare a list of PNs showing the differences in quantities, amounts and profit rates, and sorted in a way that highlights the variances.”

 

At present, we do not have a business plan or budget defined at part-number (PN) level. The planned figure ((Apr 24 – Mar 25) / 12 × 9) represents an aggregate financial plan, not a PN-based sales or margin plan. 
As a result, we can only provide is a direct PN-to-plan comparison with the same period the year before, but please keep in mind this would require the following assumptions:

 

A PN-level comparison can only be made against a historical period, not directly against the plan.

  Such a comparison does not isolate sales composition effects (model mix) from other drivers, including:

*	Warranty volume fluctuations
*	Seasonality (e.g. winter wear parts, summer service items)
*	Part lifecycle effects (e.g. declining RT parts, ageing vehicle parc)
*	Campaigns (which we did a lot last year)
*	Stock optimisation effects (stock rebalancing, a lot of DB’s adjust their MOS level due to various reasons)

 

Unless you advise otherwise, I will proceed with the analysis based on the same historical reference period.

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Dear Yoshimoto-san,



Please find below clarification on your questions:

 

*	Annual support
	Yes, the support is included in the current business plan and is provided on an annual basis.
*	Timing of the MOU
	Historically, the MOU is signed prior to the customer placing a scrap order. The rationale is that the actual need for support can vary depending on the distributor’s circumstances and order planning, therefore the MOU is concluded when the support is effectively required.
*	Order records / ceilings
	Each customer is eligible to place PRD orders up to a maximum value of €80,000. When the full €80,000 is ordered, a support amount of €20,000 is granted in the form of a credit note. With this MOU distributor get’s 25% of it’s initial PRD order. So if the distributor places an order of €40,000 customer receives  a support amount of 10,000€

Currently, their SOR is scheduled as follows:

Customer places the order on Tuesday, Sales approves it and the order must be visible in the order screen by 11:30 a.m. on Wednesday at the latest.

The warehouse can print the SOR and starts picking. This can remain the same for us.

The SOR is normally packed and complete by the following Wednesday at the latest.

*	What if the packed SOR consists of several full shipments?
*	What if an extra shipment is added, for example PRD order or Acc?
*	What about a residual shipment, for example 4 loading metres, will this remain for a whole week?

Bear in mind that we probably reserve two large zones for other customers such as Israel, which leaves us with six zones for other customers. 

If shipments for the UK remain for several days, this can cause enormous space problems in the shipping zone and cause us problems for other customers.

 

When we think about it, a fixed collection day for SOR is not so obvious. 

As we currently operate, a shipment never stays for a full week but is collected within a few days.

subject: turnover paradox
body_preview:
Hi Hadi,

Sure — here’s a scientific/economic framing you can use to make the “5% vs 2% inflation” argument feel principled (not just commercial complaining), and it will land well with Japanese HQ because it’s grounded in standard microeconomics + industrial organization.

________________________________

1) “Real price increase” and demand response (Marshall)

Alfred Marshall (foundational microeconomics) formalized that demand responds to the real price, not the nominal price.

*	If inflation ≈ 2% and we raise list prices 5%, then we’re effectively imposing a ~3% real price increase.
*	A real price increase shifts the customer along the demand curve → quantity demanded falls depending on price elasticity.

Management-friendly logic:

“A 5% increase is not ‘keeping up with costs’ when CPI is 2%. It is a real increase, so the demand response is expected, not incidental.”

________________________________

2) Price elasticity and revenue risk (Lerner & basic IO)

The elasticity rule (standard in industrial organization) is:

*	If demand is inelastic (|ε| < 1): raising price tends to raise revenue.
*	If demand is elastic (|ε| > 1): raising price can reduce revenue.

In aftermarket parts, you typically have a mix:

*	Captive parts → more inelastic
*	Wear/competitive parts → more elastic due to IAM alternatives

This ties directly to the Lerner Index (Abba Lerner):

Market power (ability to mark up price) depends on how elastic demand is.

So the scientific point is:

*	You can raise price where demand is inelastic
*	But raising price uniformly across elastic categories invites substitution and can destroy long-run profit pools.

________________________________

3) Substitution and cross-price elasticity (Hicks/Slutsky tradition)

Even if the vehicle “must be repaired,” the buyer can substitute:

*	Genuine → IAM
*	Dealer repair → independent garage
*	Immediate repair → delayed repair / partial repair

Economics breaks this into:

*	Own-price elasticity (our price ↑ → our quantity ↓)
*	Cross-price elasticity (our price ↑ → IAM quantity ↑)

That’s textbook consumer theory (Hicks/Slutsky era): higher relative prices drive substitution toward the closest alternatives.

HQ-friendly line:

“A list increase does not only reduce quantity; it reallocates volume to substitutes (IAM), accelerating genuine parts share loss.”

________________________________

4) “Price pass-through” is incomplete in the channel (double marginalization – Spengler)

This is extremely relevant for your DB chain.

In a vertical channel (OEM → DB → Dealer → End customer), a price increase upstream is not cleanly passed through because each layer has its own margin constraints.

This is classic “double marginalization” (Spengler, 1950):

*	Each layer adds markup
*	If upstream price rises, downstream either:

	*	raises retail price (risking demand loss), or
	*	absorbs part of the increase (margin compression), or
	*	switches to substitute products (IAM)

So, scientifically:

*	A 5% OEM increase can become a larger effective retail shock, OR it can force DB/dealer margin compression, which triggers IAM switching.

Simple explanation to include:

“In a multi-layer distribution system, price increases amplify demand loss unless coordination mechanisms exist.”

________________________________

5) “Reference price” and perceived fairness (Kahneman & Tversky; Thaler)

Even if the “economic” impact seems small, the behavioral impact can be larger.

Research in behavioral economics shows customers react strongly when:

*	increases exceed what they view as “cost justified”
*	increases exceed general inflation

body_preview:
Dear Yoshimoto-san,

 

Following a brief discussion with Masumi-san yesterday, he suggested that I discuss the pricing revision directly with you.

As instructed last Monday, I prepared a first draft based on a 5% increase on current prices, instead of the previously discussed 3%. I have applied the same methodology and logic as in the 3% scenario.

Below, please find my initial observations and assumptions on the first draft. These are intended as preliminary remarks, and I would welcome your guidance on how you would like to proceed and when it would be convenient to discuss the revision in more detail in the office or via a teams call.

 

*	I focused the increase generally on class C,D,F for  PR00  mostly to increase as this is a broad group of parts for which ISZE feels there is not a lot of competition and are quite captive meaning limited competitive pressure.
*	For Israel, UMI we did a 4,6% increase for competitive parts as we believe they don’t use genuine Isuzu parts after warranty period. UMI has a very low competive parts share and they have their own aftermarket brand.
*	For Israel, UTI we focused the increase on class C ,as we know they are sensitive for class D & V
*	What do we do with the prices that drop? The last years, for the parts that had a low price using the formula, we increased them to the same level but this gives an anomaly in the applied formula.
	Given the fact that ISZE needs to track everything this causes some sort of deviation between “theory” and “practice” 
*	For Israel I also focused to increase on class P to put a significant increase, which are body parts and seen as captive especially in ‘developed’ countries.
*	For CIS countries as we didn’t increase the prices last year and they are basically a dealer where most of our sales captures vehicles in their warranty period and have a low share after that period, I increased with 5% as they mentioned they have a lot of parallel import from China
*	For KIMA I await management discussions. In the past we agreed on 19% GM so they could purchase some genuine parts sourced from ISZE to keep their business alive. If we increase that to our recently calculated expanded break-even (see e-mail attached) sales would probably vanish (it’s been a tiny portion anyway this CY with 44K€ order amount)
*	These figures are lower than our sales figures as my simulation does not include engines, Shell products, replaced by asm or production discontinued, no surcharges,…
	Compared to total sales it is in line with the previous years

 

 

Kind regards,

Helo Masumi,

Given the fact that our discount rate for JP sourced parts which affect 100% of our CV parts and roughly 20% of our LCV parts can you please advise on the following and you also advised to add 5% on top of the current prices:

Is my understanding correct that turnover is the most important factor, and we ignore the drop in gross margin for JP sourced parts (which mainly affects CV?)
Or do you want a cumulative effect and keep our gross margin?



From an execution point of view, I can do the simulation exercise with the old discount rate and that we just add 5% as a recovery measure and later ISZE management can check with finance department and / or JP later on for new gross margin and profit KPI’s?

Please let me know if this approach is acceptable, or if you would recommend an alternative. Any guidance to ensure consistency and avoid rework later on would be highly appreciated.

 

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym

Subject: Pricing revision

 

Dear Masumi,

Please find here the first draft of the revision proposal, which is delayed as you know because the pricing revision file was too incomplete to start a simulation.(see first attachment)

 

*	As per your request please find attached a simulation with a 3+% increase, it’s been a while since we discussed this topic.
	Is the 3%+- increase from ISZE management still valid?
*	I focused the increase generally on class C (PR00 + Israel) mostly to increase as this is a broad group of parts for which ISZE feels there is not a lot of competition and are quite captive meaning limited competitive pressure.
*	What do we do with the prices that drop? The last years, for the parts that had a low price using the formula, we increased them to the same level but this gives an anomaly in the applied formula.
	Given the fact that ISZE needs to track everything this causes some sort of deviation between “theory” and “practice” 
*	For Israel I also focused to increase on class P to put a significant increase, which are body parts and seen as captive especially in ‘developed’ countries.
*	For CIS countries as we didn’t increase the prices last year and they are basically a dealer where most of our sales captures vehicles in their warranty period and have a low share after that period, I increased with 5% as they mentioned they have a lot of parallel import from China
*	For KIMA I await management discussions. In the past we agreed on 19% GM so they could purchase some genuine parts sourced from ISZE to keep their business alive. If we increase that to our recently calculated expanded break-even (see e-mail attached) sales would probably vanish (it’s been a tiny portion anyway this CY with 44K€ order amount)
*	These figures are lower than our sales figures as my simulation does not include engines, Shell products, replaced by asm or production discontinued, no surcharges,…
	Compared to total sales it is in line with the previous years
*	Regarding the price structure file I am still waiting for your feedback via teams from 4/12 
*	As we are nearing down on our deadline of 01/02/2026, Can you please advise if ISZE can communicate a general weighted increase of +-3% to the customers
	At the moment no customers have asked anything besides some if we would still reach the 01/01/2026 deadline and secondly please keep in mind ISZE had the tradition of providing preliminary price files 
	for review / comment +-30 days in advance. To counter this we advise the weighted increase to the customers in the first week of Janua

Dear Suzuki-san,

Best wishes for the new year.

Allow me to explain the procedure / background a bit more in detail.

For shipments from ISZE to Kazakhstan, Armenia and Ukraine, a Certificate of Origin (COO) is required. Without this document the goods may be blocked at customs, as it is a mandatory import requirement in these countries.

In addition, the underlying reason can differ per country—for example, Ukraine requires clear proof of origin to ensure that the shipped parts are not of Russian origin.

Because one shipment can contain parts with different origins, ISZE must be able to demonstrate the country of origin per invoice line (part number level). Origins from Japan, Thailand and China are already covered by existing declarations.

For parts with other origins we can use the following methods:

1.	IML/IMIT master COO declaration list (preferred): a signed list as per your attachment. This is the most efficient option, as it covers many part numbers at once and avoids manual checks. The list is valid for two years.
2.	Purchase invoice evidence: if a part is not included in the master list, we use the supplier sales invoice (IML/IMIT invoice) as proof of origin. In practice this can be challenging because some invoices are only available as scanned copies, pages may be missing, or older invoices may be difficult to retrieve.
3.	Specific declaration (last resort): if neither the master list nor invoice evidence is available, we request a signed declaration for the specific part numbers on IML/IMIT letterhead. (attached)

 

We managed to get this COO issued and it has already been accepted by customs.

Please note that these cases are always time-critical. The COO procedure can only be started once the sales invoice has been created, while physical shipments can reach the Ukrainian border within approximately four days.

If the COO is not available upon arrival, the shipment will be held at the border and demurrage costs will apply, which would be charged to the customer. We therefore aim to prevent this situation wherever possible.



I hope this helps and gives you a better understanding.

Kind regards,

Jérôme Van der Pluym
